# MiniScheme Device API 1.10.0

The procedures a MiniScheme app can call on the device (ESP32 firmware) and in the
WASM simulator, grouped by component. Device procedures are named
`component-function`; the language core keeps the standard Scheme names.
See [README.md](README.md) for the versioning rules, how an app declares the API it
needs, the hooks the firmware calls, and the app framework.

- API version: **1.10.0**
- Entries: 342 implemented, 67 reserved, 27 older names (aliases)
- Extensions: `esp32` 1.0.0 (ESP32 chip features (Espressif SoC only))

Conventions: `[x]` is an optional argument, `x ...` any number of them. A line
`; => value` in an example shows the value as `write` prints it; these examples are
run by the test suite on a VM configured like the firmware.

<a id="api-when"></a>
#### `when`

`(when test body ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Evaluate body ... in order when test is true (anything but #f).

**Returns:** The value of the last body expression; void when test is #f.

```scheme
(define level 80)
(when (> level 50) 'warned)          ; => warned
(void? (when (> level 90) 'alarm))   ; => #t
```

<a id="api-unless"></a>
#### `unless`

`(unless test body ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Evaluate body ... in order when test is #f.

**Returns:** The value of the last body expression; void when test is true.

```scheme
(define connected #f)
(unless connected 'offline)          ; => offline
(void? (unless #t 'never))           ; => #t
```

<a id="api-and"></a>
#### `and`

`(and test ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Evaluate tests left to right, stopping at the first #f.

**Returns:** #f at the first false test (the rest is not evaluated), else the value of the last test; #t with no tests.

```scheme
(and 1 2 3)                          ; => 3
(and (> 5 1) (< 5 3))                ; => #f
(define lst '())
(and (pair? lst) (car lst))          ; => #f
(and)                                ; => #t
```

<a id="api-or"></a>
#### `or`

`(or test ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Evaluate tests left to right, stopping at the first true value.

**Returns:** The first value that is not #f (the rest is not evaluated); #f when every test is #f or there are none.

```scheme
(or #f 2 (car '()))                  ; => 2
(or (memq 'x '(a b)) 'none)          ; => none
(or)                                 ; => #f
```

<a id="api-cond"></a>
#### `cond`

`(cond (test expr ...) ... [else expr ...])`

*since 1.0.0*

Evaluate the clause of the first true test; (test => proc) calls proc on the test value.

**Returns:** The value of the last expression of the selected clause; the test value for a clause without expressions; proc's result for =>. Void when no clause matches and there is no else.

```scheme
(define (sign n) (cond ((< n 0) 'negative) ((= n 0) 'zero) (else 'positive)))
(sign -4)                            ; => negative
(cond ((assv 2 '((1 . one) (2 . two))) => cdr) (else 'none))  ; => two
(void? (cond (#f 1)))                ; => #t
```

<a id="api-if"></a>
#### `if`

`(if test then [else])`

*since 1.0.0*

Evaluate then when test is true (anything but #f, even 0 and ()), else the else branch.

**Returns:** The value of the branch taken; void when test is #f and else is omitted.

```scheme
(if (> 3 2) 'yes 'no)                ; => yes
(if '() 'true 'false)                ; => true
(void? (if #f #f))                   ; => #t
```

<a id="api-lambda"></a>
#### `lambda`

`(lambda params body ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Create a procedure. params is (a b ...), (a b . rest) or one symbol bound to the list of all arguments.

**Returns:** A procedure (a closure over the variables in scope).

Calls are not arity-checked: a missing argument reads as void and extra arguments are ignored.

```scheme
(define add (lambda (a b) (+ a b)))
(add 2 3)                            ; => 5
((lambda (first . rest) rest) 1 2 3) ; => (2 3)
((lambda args (length args)) 'a 'b)  ; => 2
```

<a id="api-let"></a>
#### `let`

`(let ((var val) ...) body ...) / (let name ((var val) ...) body ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Bind local variables in parallel and evaluate body; the named form binds name to a loop procedure.

**Returns:** The value of the last body expression.

```scheme
(let ((x 2) (y 3)) (* x y))          ; => 6
(let loop ((i 0) (acc '()))
  (if (= i 3) (reverse acc) (loop (+ i 1) (cons i acc))))  ; => (0 1 2)
```

<a id="api-let_2a"></a>
#### `let*`

`(let* ((var val) ...) body ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Bind local variables sequentially (each init sees the previous ones) and evaluate body.

**Returns:** The value of the last body expression.

```scheme
(let* ((w 4) (area (* w w))) area)   ; => 16
(let* () 'empty)                     ; => empty
```

<a id="api-define"></a>
#### `define`

`(define var val) / (define (name args...) body...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Bind a global (at top level) or a local (at the start of a body); the second form defines a procedure.

**Returns:** At top level the name as a symbol (a redefinition replaces the value); an internal define returns void.

```scheme
(define limit 10)                    ; => limit
(define (square n) (* n n))
(square 7)                           ; => 49
(define (hyp2 a b) (define s (+ (square a) (square b))) s)
(hyp2 3 4)                           ; => 25
```

<a id="api-set_21"></a>
#### `set!`

`(set! var val)`

*since 1.0.0*

Assign a new value to an existing local or global variable.

**Returns:** Void. An error "set!: unbound variable" when var is neither a local nor a defined global.

```scheme
(define count 0)
(set! count (+ count 1))
count                                ; => 1
(set! no-such-var 5)                 ; => error: unbound variable
```

<a id="api-begin"></a>
#### `begin`

`(begin expr ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Evaluate expressions in order; at top level its definitions stay global.

**Returns:** The value of the last expression; void for (begin).

```scheme
(define total 0)
(begin (set! total (+ total 5)) (set! total (* total 2)) total)  ; => 10
(void? (begin))                      ; => #t
```

<a id="api-quote"></a>
#### `quote`

`(quote datum) / 'datum`

*since 1.0.0*

Return datum without evaluating it.

**Returns:** datum itself: a symbol, list, vector or constant. Quoted data is a constant: do not mutate it (it may live in the read-only Code ROM).

```scheme
(quote (+ 1 2))                      ; => (+ 1 2)
'(a b c)                             ; => (a b c)
(car '(red green))                   ; => red
'#(1 2)                              ; => #(1 2)
```

<a id="api-define-syntax"></a>
#### `define-syntax`

`(define-syntax name (syntax-rules ...))`

*since 1.0.0*

Define a syntax-rules macro, expanded at compile time; locals introduced by the template are renamed.

**Returns:** The macro name as a symbol. A use that matches no rule is a compile error "no syntax-rules pattern matched".

Template symbols that are pattern variables, literals, special forms or defined globals are kept as written; other symbols the template introduces get fresh names.

```scheme
(define-syntax swap!
  (syntax-rules () ((_ a b) (let ((tmp a)) (set! a b) (set! b tmp)))))
(define x 1)
(define y 2)
(swap! x y)
(list x y)                           ; => (2 1)
```

<a id="api-syntax-rules"></a>
#### `syntax-rules`

`(syntax-rules (literal ...) (pattern template) ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

The rules of define-syntax: the first pattern matching the form selects its template; x ... repeats.

**Returns:** A macro transformer; valid only as the second operand of define-syntax (elsewhere it is an unbound variable).

The keyword position of a pattern is ignored (write _). Literals match only the same symbol.

```scheme
(define-syntax my-or
  (syntax-rules ()
    ((_) #f)
    ((_ e) e)
    ((_ e r ...) (let ((t e)) (if t t (my-or r ...))))))
(my-or #f #f 3)                      ; => 3
```

<a id="api-define-macro"></a>
#### `define-macro`

`(define-macro (name args...) body...) / (define-macro name proc)`

*since 1.0.0*

Define a non-hygienic macro: body builds the expansion from the unevaluated operands, at compile time.

**Returns:** The macro name as a symbol.

```scheme
(define-macro (inc! var . by)
  (list 'set! var (list '+ var (if (null? by) 1 (car by)))))
(define n 5)
(inc! n)
(inc! n 10)
n                                    ; => 16
```

<a id="api-include-bytes"></a>
#### `include-bytes`

`(include-bytes path)`

*since 1.0.0*

The file's bytes as a string. Compiled code gets them at compile time (embedded in the image), e.g. fonts.

**Returns:** A string of the file's bytes (NUL bytes included). A missing file is a compile error "include-bytes: cannot read file".

The path is relative to the working directory of the compiler (tools/build_apps.py: the repository root). The example needs a font file the test VM lacks.

```scheme
(define digits (include-bytes "fonts/digits-48.mfnt"))
(font-register! 3 digits)            ; => #t
(include-bytes "no-such-file.bin")   ; => error: include-bytes: cannot read file
```

<a id="api-_2b"></a>
#### `+`

`(+ z ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the sum of the arguments (0 if no arguments).

**Returns:** The sum: an exact integer (a bignum when it overflows the fixnum range), or a flonum when any argument is a flonum; an error when an argument is not a number.

Numbers are exact integers (fixnums, promoted to bignums automatically when a result leaves the fixnum range: 29 bits on the 32-bit device and WASM, 61 bits on a 64-bit PC) or inexact flonums (C doubles). There are no rationals or complex numbers. A flonum argument makes the result a flonum. `write` prints a flonum with up to 15 significant digits and a trailing `.0` when it is integral (`3.5`, `2.0`, `0.333333333333333`).

```scheme
(+ 1 2 3)            ; => 6
(+ 1 2.5)            ; => 3.5
(+)                  ; => 0
(define big (expt 2 62))
(+ big 1)            ; => 4611686018427387905
(+ 1 "2")            ; => error: expected number
```

<a id="api--"></a>
#### `-`

`(- z1 [z2 ...])`

*since 1.0.0*

Subtract following arguments from z1, or negate z1.

**Returns:** The difference, or the negation of z1 alone: exact integer or flonum as for `+`; an error with no argument or when an argument is not a number.

```scheme
(- 10 1 2)           ; => 7
(- 5)                ; => -5
(- 0.5 1)            ; => -0.5
(-)                  ; => error: requires at least 1 argument
```

<a id="api-_2a"></a>
#### `*`

`(* z ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the product of the arguments (1 if no arguments).

**Returns:** The product: an exact integer (a bignum when it overflows), or a flonum when any argument is a flonum; an error when an argument is not a number.

```scheme
(* 2 3 4)            ; => 24
(* 2 1.5)            ; => 3.0
(*)                  ; => 1
(define n (expt 10 10))
(* n n)              ; => 100000000000000000000
```

<a id="api-_2f"></a>
#### `/`

`(/ z1 [z2 ...])`

*since 1.0.0*

Divide z1 by the following arguments, or return 1/z1. An inexact quotient of integers is a flonum (no rationals).

**Returns:** An exact integer when every division is exact, otherwise a flonum; an error "division by zero" when a divisor is 0 or 0.0, or when an argument is not a number.

```scheme
(/ 8 2)              ; => 4
(/ 7 2)              ; => 3.5
(/ 1 3)              ; => 0.333333333333333
(/ 2)                ; => 0.5
(/ 7 0)              ; => error: division by zero
```

<a id="api-_3c"></a>
#### `<`

`(< x1 x2 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if numbers are strictly monotonically increasing.

**Returns:** #t or #f; exact and inexact numbers compare by value. With fewer than two arguments #t. An error when a compared argument is not a number (comparison stops at the first #f).

```scheme
(< 1 2 3)            ; => #t
(< 1 3 2)            ; => #f
(< 1 2.5)            ; => #t
(< 1 'a)             ; => error: expected numbers
```

<a id="api-_3e"></a>
#### `>`

`(> x1 x2 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if numbers are strictly monotonically decreasing.

**Returns:** #t or #f, as for `<`; an error when a compared argument is not a number.

```scheme
(> 3 2 1)            ; => #t
(> 3 3)              ; => #f
(> 2.5 2)            ; => #t
```

<a id="api-_3c_3d"></a>
#### `<=`

`(<= x1 x2 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if numbers are monotonically non-decreasing.

**Returns:** #t or #f, as for `<`; an error when a compared argument is not a number.

```scheme
(<= 1 1 2)           ; => #t
(<= 2 1)             ; => #f
(let ((t 21.5)) (<= 18 t 25))  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-_3e_3d"></a>
#### `>=`

`(>= x1 x2 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if numbers are monotonically non-increasing.

**Returns:** #t or #f, as for `<`; an error when a compared argument is not a number.

```scheme
(>= 3 3 1)           ; => #t
(>= 1 2)             ; => #f
```

<a id="api-_3d"></a>
#### `=`

`(= z1 z2 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if all numbers are numerically equal.

**Returns:** #t or #f; an exact and an inexact number are equal when their values are (`(= 1 1.0)` is #t). An error when a compared argument is not a number.

```scheme
(= 2 2 2)            ; => #t
(= 1 1.0)            ; => #t
(= 1 2)              ; => #f
```

<a id="api-modulo"></a>
#### `modulo`

`(modulo n1 n2)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return n1 modulo n2: the remainder with the sign of n2.

**Returns:** An exact integer with the sign of n2 (floor division); an error when an argument is not an exact integer (flonums are refused) or n2 is 0.

```scheme
(modulo 13 4)        ; => 1
(modulo -7 2)        ; => 1
(modulo 7 -2)        ; => -1
(modulo 7 0)         ; => error: division by zero
```

<a id="api-remainder"></a>
#### `remainder`

`(remainder n1 n2)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the remainder of dividing n1 by n2, with the sign of n1.

**Returns:** An exact integer with the sign of n1 (truncating division); an error when an argument is not an exact integer or n2 is 0.

```scheme
(remainder 17 5)     ; => 2
(remainder -7 2)     ; => -1
(remainder 17 -5)    ; => 2
```

<a id="api-quotient"></a>
#### `quotient`

`(quotient n1 n2)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the integer quotient of dividing n1 by n2, truncated towards zero.

**Returns:** An exact integer (bignums allowed); an error when an argument is not an exact integer (`(quotient 7.0 2)` fails) or n2 is 0.

```scheme
(quotient 17 5)      ; => 3
(quotient -7 2)      ; => -3
(quotient 7.0 2)     ; => error: expected 2 integers
```

<a id="api-abs"></a>
#### `abs`

`(abs x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the absolute value of x.

**Returns:** A number of the same exactness as x; an error when x is not a number.

```scheme
(abs -5)             ; => 5
(abs -2.5)           ; => 2.5
(abs 3)              ; => 3
```

<a id="api-sqrt"></a>
#### `sqrt`

`(sqrt z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the square root of z as a flonum.

**Returns:** A flonum, also for exact arguments (`(sqrt 16)` is 4.0); an error when z is negative or not a number.

```scheme
(sqrt 16)            ; => 4.0
(sqrt 2)             ; => 1.4142135623731
(sqrt -1)            ; => error: negative number
```

<a id="api-sin"></a>
#### `sin`

`(sin z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the sine of z (in radians).

**Returns:** A flonum; an error when z is not a number.

```scheme
(sin 0)              ; => 0.0
(sin 1.5707963267949)  ; => 1.0
```

<a id="api-cos"></a>
#### `cos`

`(cos z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the cosine of z (in radians).

**Returns:** A flonum; an error when z is not a number.

```scheme
(cos 0)              ; => 1.0
(cos 3.14159265358979)  ; => -1.0
```

<a id="api-tan"></a>
#### `tan`

`(tan z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the tangent of z (in radians).

**Returns:** A flonum; an error when z is not a number.

```scheme
(tan 0)              ; => 0.0
(tan 0.785398163397448)  ; => 0.999999999999999
```

<a id="api-asin"></a>
#### `asin`

`(asin z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the arcsine of z, in radians.

**Returns:** A flonum in [-pi/2, pi/2]; NaN when z is outside [-1, 1]; an error when z is not a number.

```scheme
(asin 1)             ; => 1.5707963267949
(asin 0)             ; => 0.0
```

<a id="api-acos"></a>
#### `acos`

`(acos z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the arccosine of z, in radians.

**Returns:** A flonum in [0, pi]; NaN when z is outside [-1, 1]; an error when z is not a number.

```scheme
(acos 1)             ; => 0.0
(acos -1)            ; => 3.14159265358979
```

<a id="api-atan"></a>
#### `atan`

`(atan y [x])`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the arctangent of y, or with x the angle of the point (x, y) (atan2).

**Returns:** A flonum in radians: in [-pi/2, pi/2] for one argument, in [-pi, pi] for two; an error when an argument is not a number.

```scheme
(atan 1)             ; => 0.785398163397448
(atan 1 0)           ; => 1.5707963267949
(atan 0 -1)          ; => 3.14159265358979
```

<a id="api-exp"></a>
#### `exp`

`(exp z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return e raised to the power of z.

**Returns:** A flonum; an error when z is not a number.

```scheme
(exp 0)              ; => 1.0
(exp 1)              ; => 2.71828182845905
```

<a id="api-log"></a>
#### `log`

`(log z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the natural logarithm of z.

**Returns:** A flonum; an error when z is not positive or not a number. There is no two-argument form: divide by `(log base)`.

```scheme
(log 1)              ; => 0.0
(log 100)            ; => 4.60517018598809
(/ (log 1000) (log 10))  ; => 3.0
(log 0)              ; => error: expected positive number
```

<a id="api-expt"></a>
#### `expt`

`(expt z1 z2)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return z1 raised to the power of z2.

**Returns:** An exact integer (bignum when large) for an exact base and a non-negative exact exponent; otherwise a flonum (also for a negative exact exponent); an error when an argument is not a number.

```scheme
(expt 2 10)          ; => 1024
(expt 2 100)         ; => 1267650600228229401496703205376
(expt 2 -1)          ; => 0.5
(expt 4 0.5)         ; => 2.0
```

<a id="api-floor"></a>
#### `floor`

`(floor x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the largest integer <= x.

**Returns:** x itself for an exact integer, an integral flonum for a flonum (use `inexact->exact` for an exact result); an error when x is not a number.

```scheme
(floor 2.5)          ; => 2.0
(floor -2.5)         ; => -3.0
(floor 7)            ; => 7
(inexact->exact (floor 2.7))  ; => 2
```

<a id="api-ceiling"></a>
#### `ceiling`

`(ceiling x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the smallest integer >= x.

**Returns:** x itself for an exact integer, an integral flonum for a flonum; an error when x is not a number.

```scheme
(ceiling 2.1)        ; => 3.0
(ceiling -2.1)       ; => -2.0
(ceiling 4)          ; => 4
```

<a id="api-round"></a>
#### `round`

`(round x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Round x to the nearest integer; halves round away from zero (2.5 -> 3.0).

**Returns:** x itself for an exact integer, an integral flonum for a flonum; an error when x is not a number.

Unlike R7RS (round half to even), halves round away from zero (C `round`).

```scheme
(round 2.4)          ; => 2.0
(round 2.5)          ; => 3.0
(round -2.5)         ; => -3.0
(round 7)            ; => 7
```

<a id="api-truncate"></a>
#### `truncate`

`(truncate x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Truncate x towards zero.

**Returns:** x itself for an exact integer, an integral flonum for a flonum; an error when x is not a number.

```scheme
(truncate 2.7)       ; => 2.0
(truncate -2.7)      ; => -2.0
(truncate 5)         ; => 5
```

<a id="api-exact_3f"></a>
#### `exact?`

`(exact? z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if z is an exact number (fixnum or bignum).

**Returns:** #t for an exact integer, #f for a flonum; #f (no error) for a non-number.

```scheme
(exact? 1)           ; => #t
(exact? 1.0)         ; => #f
(exact? (expt 2 100))  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-inexact_3f"></a>
#### `inexact?`

`(inexact? z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if z is an inexact number (flonum).

**Returns:** #t for a flonum, #f for an exact integer; #f (no error) for a non-number.

```scheme
(inexact? 1.5)       ; => #t
(inexact? 2)         ; => #f
```

<a id="api-exact-_3einexact"></a>
#### `exact->inexact`

`(exact->inexact z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert an exact number to an inexact flonum.

**Returns:** A flonum (a flonum argument is returned as a flonum of the same value; large bignums lose precision); an error when z is not a number.

```scheme
(exact->inexact 3)   ; => 3.0
(exact->inexact 1.5) ; => 1.5
(/ (exact->inexact 1) 4)  ; => 0.25
```

<a id="api-inexact-_3eexact"></a>
#### `inexact->exact`

`(inexact->exact z)`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert z to an exact integer, rounding a flonum to the nearest integer (halves away from zero).

**Returns:** An exact integer: z itself when exact, otherwise the flonum rounded to the nearest integer (no rationals), a bignum when large; an error when z is not a number, or is a NaN or infinity.

```scheme
(inexact->exact 2.6)  ; => 3
(inexact->exact 2.5)  ; => 3
(inexact->exact -2.4) ; => -2
(inexact->exact 7)    ; => 7
```

<a id="api-max"></a>
#### `max`

`(max x1 x2 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

The largest argument.

**Returns:** The largest argument itself, unconverted: `(max 3 2.0)` is the exact 3 (no inexact contagion, unlike R7RS); an error with no argument or a non-number.

```scheme
(max 1 5 3)          ; => 5
(max 1 2.0)          ; => 2.0
(max 3 2.0)          ; => 3
(max)                ; => error: requires at least 1 argument
```

<a id="api-min"></a>
#### `min`

`(min x1 x2 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

The smallest argument.

**Returns:** The smallest argument itself, unconverted (no inexact contagion); an error with no argument or a non-number.

```scheme
(min 4 1 3)          ; => 1
(min 1.0 2)          ; => 1.0
(min 0 (max 255 300))  ; => 0
```

<a id="api-cons"></a>
#### `cons`

`(cons obj1 obj2)`

*since 1.0.0*

Construct a new pair with car obj1 and cdr obj2.

**Returns:** A newly allocated pair; an error unless exactly 2 arguments are given.

```scheme
(cons 1 2)           ; => (1 . 2)
(cons 1 '(2 3))      ; => (1 2 3)
(cons 'a '())        ; => (a)
```

<a id="api-car"></a>
#### `car`

`(car pair)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the first element of pair.

**Returns:** The car of pair; an error when pair is not a pair (including the empty list).

```scheme
(car '(1 2 3))       ; => 1
(car '((a . b) c))   ; => (a . b)
(car '())            ; => error: requires a pair
```

<a id="api-cdr"></a>
#### `cdr`

`(cdr pair)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the second element of pair.

**Returns:** The cdr of pair (the rest of a list); an error when pair is not a pair.

```scheme
(cdr '(1 2 3))       ; => (2 3)
(cdr '(1 . 2))       ; => 2
(cdr '())            ; => error: requires a pair
```

<a id="api-set-car_21"></a>
#### `set-car!`

`(set-car! pair obj)`

*since 1.0.0*

Mutate the car field of pair.

**Returns:** Void; an error when pair is not a pair or is a quoted literal in the read-only code image.

Quoted literals of an app loaded from the read-only code image (XIP) cannot be modified: mutating one raises "cannot modify a literal constant". Mutate freshly allocated data (list, vector, cons, make-vector) instead.

```scheme
(define p (cons 1 2))
(set-car! p 9)
p                    ; => (9 . 2)
```

<a id="api-set-cdr_21"></a>
#### `set-cdr!`

`(set-cdr! pair obj)`

*since 1.0.0*

Mutate the cdr field of pair.

**Returns:** Void; an error when pair is not a pair or is a quoted literal in the read-only code image.

Quoted literals of an app loaded from the read-only code image (XIP) cannot be modified: mutating one raises "cannot modify a literal constant". Mutate freshly allocated data (list, vector, cons, make-vector) instead.

```scheme
(define p (list 1 2))
(set-cdr! p '(3 4))
p                    ; => (1 3 4)
```

<a id="api-pair_3f"></a>
#### `pair?`

`(pair? obj)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return #t if obj is a pair, #f otherwise.

**Returns:** #t or #f; the empty list is not a pair.

```scheme
(pair? '(1))         ; => #t
(pair? '(1 . 2))     ; => #t
(pair? '())          ; => #f
(pair? (vector 1))   ; => #f
```

<a id="api-null_3f"></a>
#### `null?`

`(null? obj)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return #t if obj is empty list (), #f otherwise.

**Returns:** #t only for the empty list; #f for anything else (also #f and "").

```scheme
(null? '())          ; => #t
(null? '(1))         ; => #f
(null? #f)           ; => #f
```

<a id="api-list"></a>
#### `list`

`(list obj ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return a newly allocated list of its arguments.

**Returns:** A new proper list; `()` with no arguments.

```scheme
(list 1 2 3)         ; => (1 2 3)
(list 'a "b" (+ 1 2))  ; => (a "b" 3)
(list)               ; => ()
```

<a id="api-length"></a>
#### `length`

`(length list)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the number of elements in list.

**Returns:** An exact integer; an error "not a proper list" for an improper list or a non-list.

```scheme
(length '(1 2 3))    ; => 3
(length '())         ; => 0
(length '(1 . 2))    ; => error: not a proper list
```

<a id="api-reverse"></a>
#### `reverse`

`(reverse list)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return a newly allocated list with elements in reverse order.

**Returns:** A new list; the argument is not changed. Not checked: the tail of an improper list is dropped and a non-list gives `()`.

```scheme
(reverse '(1 2 3))   ; => (3 2 1)
(reverse '())        ; => ()
```

<a id="api-append"></a>
#### `append`

`(append list ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Concatenate lists into a single list.

**Returns:** A list whose elements are copied from all arguments but the last, which is shared (it may be any object, giving an improper list); `()` with no arguments. Not checked: a non-list argument before the last counts as empty.

```scheme
(append '(1) '(2 3) '(4))  ; => (1 2 3 4)
(append '(1 2) 3)    ; => (1 2 . 3)
(append)             ; => ()
```

<a id="api-map"></a>
#### `map`

`(map proc list ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Apply proc element-wise across lists and return list of results.

**Returns:** A new list of the results, in order; with several lists it stops at the end of the shortest. An error with no list or more than 4 lists, when proc is not a procedure, or when proc raises one.

```scheme
(map (lambda (x) (* x x)) '(1 2 3))  ; => (1 4 9)
(map + '(1 2 3) '(10 20))  ; => (11 22)
(map car '((a 1) (b 2)))  ; => (a b)
```

<a id="api-filter"></a>
#### `filter`

`(filter pred list)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return a list of elements satisfying predicate pred.

**Returns:** A new list of the elements for which pred returns a true value, in their original order; an error unless 2 arguments are given or when pred raises one.

```scheme
(filter (lambda (x) (> x 1)) '(1 2 3))  ; => (2 3)
(filter string? '(1 "a" b "c"))  ; => ("a" "c")
(filter pair? '())   ; => ()
```

<a id="api-fold-left"></a>
#### `fold-left`

`(fold-left proc init list)`

*since 1.0.0*

Left-associative fold: (proc ... (proc init x1) x2).

**Returns:** The last value of proc, called as (proc acc x) for each element from the left; init for an empty list. Exactly one list: an error otherwise.

```scheme
(fold-left + 0 '(1 2 3))  ; => 6
(fold-left - 0 '(1 2 3))  ; => -6
(fold-left (lambda (acc x) (cons x acc)) '() '(1 2 3))  ; => (3 2 1)
```

<a id="api-fold-right"></a>
#### `fold-right`

`(fold-right proc init list)`

*since 1.0.0*

Right-associative fold: (proc x1 (proc x2 ... init)).

**Returns:** The last value of proc, called as (proc x acc) for each element from the right; init for an empty list. Exactly one list: an error otherwise.

```scheme
(fold-right cons '() '(1 2 3))  ; => (1 2 3)
(fold-right - 0 '(1 2 3))  ; => 2
```

<a id="api-caar"></a>
#### `caar`

`(caar x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Equivalent to (car (car x)).

**Returns:** The car of the car of x; an error when x or its car is not a pair.

```scheme
(caar '((1 2) 3))    ; => 1
(caar '(1))          ; => error: requires a pair in car
```

<a id="api-cadr"></a>
#### `cadr`

`(cadr x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Equivalent to (car (cdr x)): the second element.

**Returns:** The second element of x; an error when x or its cdr is not a pair.

```scheme
(cadr '(1 2 3))      ; => 2
(cadr '(1))          ; => error: requires a pair in cdr
```

<a id="api-cdar"></a>
#### `cdar`

`(cdar x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Equivalent to (cdr (car x)).

**Returns:** The cdr of the car of x; an error when x or its car is not a pair.

```scheme
(cdar '((1 2) 3))    ; => (2)
(cdar '((a . b)))    ; => b
```

<a id="api-cddr"></a>
#### `cddr`

`(cddr x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Equivalent to (cdr (cdr x)).

**Returns:** x without its first two elements; an error when x or its cdr is not a pair.

```scheme
(cddr '(1 2 3))      ; => (3)
(cddr '(1 2))        ; => ()
```

<a id="api-list-tail"></a>
#### `list-tail`

`(list-tail list k)`

*since 1.0.0*

The list without its first k elements.

**Returns:** The k-th tail of list (shared, not copied); an error when k is not a non-negative fixnum or the list has fewer than k elements.

```scheme
(list-tail '(1 2 3 4) 2)  ; => (3 4)
(list-tail '(1 2) 2)  ; => ()
(list-tail '(1 2) 3)  ; => error: index out of range
```

<a id="api-memv"></a>
#### `memv`

`(memv x list)`

*since 1.0.0*

First tail whose car is eqv? to x, or #f.

**Returns:** The first tail of list whose car is eqv? to x (numbers compare by value and exactness), or #f; #f also when list is not a list.

```scheme
(memv 2 '(1 2 3))    ; => (2 3)
(memv 1.5 '(1 1.5 2))  ; => (1.5 2)
(memv 5 '(1 2 3))    ; => #f
```

<a id="api-assv"></a>
#### `assv`

`(assv key alist)`

*since 1.0.0*

First pair whose car is eqv? to key, or #f.

**Returns:** The first pair of alist whose car is eqv? to key, or #f; elements that are not pairs are skipped.

```scheme
(assv 2 '((1 . one) (2 . two)))  ; => (2 . two)
(assv 9 '((1 . one)))  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-cdddr"></a>
#### `cdddr`

`(cdddr x)`

*since 1.0.0*

(cdr (cdr (cdr x))): x without its first three elements.

**Returns:** The third tail of x; an error "list too short" when x has fewer than 3 pairs.

```scheme
(cdddr '(1 2 3 4))   ; => (4)
(cdddr '(1 2))       ; => error: list too short
```

<a id="api-cadddr"></a>
#### `cadddr`

`(cadddr x)`

*since 1.0.0*

Fourth element: (car (cdddr x)).

**Returns:** The fourth element of x; an error "list too short" when x has fewer than 4 elements.

```scheme
(cadddr '(1 2 3 4))  ; => 4
(cadddr '(1 2 3))    ; => error: list too short
```

<a id="api-cddddr"></a>
#### `cddddr`

`(cddddr x)`

*since 1.0.0*

(cdr (cdddr x)): x without its first four elements.

**Returns:** The fourth tail of x; an error "list too short" when x has fewer than 4 pairs.

```scheme
(cddddr '(1 2 3 4 5))  ; => (5)
(cddddr '(1 2 3 4))  ; => ()
```

<a id="api-assoc"></a>
#### `assoc`

`(assoc key alist)`

*since 1.0.0*

First pair of alist whose car is equal? to key, or #f.

**Returns:** The first pair whose car is equal? to key (strings and lists compare by content), or #f; elements that are not pairs are skipped.

```scheme
(assoc "b" '(("a" . 1) ("b" . 2)))  ; => ("b" . 2)
(assoc '(1) '(((1) . x)))  ; => ((1) . x)
(assoc "z" '(("a" . 1)))  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-assq"></a>
#### `assq`

`(assq key alist)`

*since 1.0.0*

First pair of alist whose car is eq? to key, or #f.

**Returns:** The first pair whose car is eq? to key (identity: use for symbols, small integers, booleans), or #f.

```scheme
(assq 'b '((a 1) (b 2)))  ; => (b 2)
(cadr (assq 'a '((a 1) (b 2))))  ; => 1
(assq "b" '(("b" . 2)))  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-caddr"></a>
#### `caddr`

`(caddr list)`

*since 1.0.0*

The third element.

**Returns:** The third element of list; an error "list too short" when it has fewer than 3 elements.

```scheme
(caddr '(1 2 3))     ; => 3
(caddr '(1 2))       ; => error: list too short
```

<a id="api-for-each"></a>
#### `for-each`

`(for-each proc list ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Call proc on the elements in order, for effect.

**Returns:** Void; with several lists it stops at the end of the shortest. An error with no list or more than 4 lists, when proc is not a procedure, or when proc raises one.

```scheme
(define total 0)
(for-each (lambda (x) (set! total (+ total x))) '(1 2 3))
total                ; => 6
```

<a id="api-list-ref"></a>
#### `list-ref`

`(list-ref list k)`

*since 1.0.0*

The k-th element (0-based).

**Returns:** The element at index k; an error when k is not a non-negative fixnum or is not less than the length.

```scheme
(list-ref '(a b c) 1)  ; => b
(list-ref '(a b c) 0)  ; => a
(list-ref '(a b c) 3)  ; => error: index out of range
```

<a id="api-member"></a>
#### `member`

`(member obj list)`

*since 1.0.0*

First tail of list whose car is equal? to obj, or #f.

**Returns:** The first tail whose car is equal? to obj (structural comparison), or #f; #f also when list is not a list.

```scheme
(member '(1) '((0) (1) (2)))  ; => ((1) (2))
(member "b" '("a" "b"))  ; => ("b")
(member 9 '(1 2))    ; => #f
```

<a id="api-memq"></a>
#### `memq`

`(memq obj list)`

*since 1.0.0*

First tail of list whose car is eq? to obj, or #f.

**Returns:** The first tail whose car is eq? to obj (identity: use for symbols, small integers, booleans), or #f.

```scheme
(memq 'c '(a b c d))  ; => (c d)
(memq 'z '(a b))     ; => #f
(if (memq 'red '(red green)) 'known 'unknown)  ; => known
```

<a id="api-list-sort"></a>
#### `list-sort`

`(list-sort less? list)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'list-sort)` is `#f`)*

A new list sorted by (less? a b); stable.

**Returns:** A newly allocated list of the elements of list in ascending order according to less? (a stable merge sort: equal elements keep their order; list is not changed); `()` for `()`. An error when list is not a proper list, less? is not a procedure, or less? raises one.

The argument order is R6RS `(list-sort proc list)` and SRFI 132.

```scheme
(list-sort < '(3 1 2))  ; => (1 2 3)
(list-sort string<? '("pear" "apple"))  ; => ("apple" "pear")
(list-sort (lambda (x y) (< (cdr x) (cdr y))) '((b . 2) (a . 1) (c . 2)))
; => ((a . 1) (b . 2) (c . 2))
```

<a id="api-list-index"></a>
#### `list-index`

`(list-index pred list)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'list-index)` is `#f`)*

Index of the first element satisfying pred, or #f.

**Returns:** The 0-based index of the first element for which pred returns a true value, or #f when none does; an error when list is not a list or pred raises one.

```scheme
(list-index even? '(1 3 4 5))  ; => 2
(list-index (lambda (s) (string=? s "b")) '("a" "b"))  ; => 1
(list-index zero? '(1 2))  ; => #f
```

<a id="component-vector"></a>
### Vectors (`vector`)

Fixed-length vectors.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(vector? obj)`](#api-vector_3f) | stable |
| [`(make-vector k [fill])`](#api-make-vector) | stable |
| [`(vector obj ...)`](#api-vector) | stable |
| [`(vector-length vec)`](#api-vector-length) | stable |
| [`(vector-ref vec k)`](#api-vector-ref) | stable |
| [`(vector-set! vec k obj)`](#api-vector-set_21) | stable |
| [`(vector->list vec)`](#api-vector-_3elist) | stable |
| [`(list->vector list)`](#api-list-_3evector) | stable |
| [`(vector-fill! vec fill)`](#api-vector-fill_21) | stable |

<a id="api-vector_3f"></a>
#### `vector?`

`(vector? obj)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if obj is a vector.

**Returns:** #t or #f.

```scheme
(vector? (vector 1 2))  ; => #t
(vector? '#(1 2))    ; => #t
(vector? '(1 2))     ; => #f
```

<a id="api-make-vector"></a>
#### `make-vector`

`(make-vector k [fill])`

*since 1.0.0*

Create vector of length k, filled with fill (default 0).

**Returns:** A new vector of k elements, all fill (0 when omitted); an error when k is not a non-negative fixnum.

```scheme
(make-vector 3 'x)   ; => #(x x x)
(make-vector 2)      ; => #(0 0)
(make-vector -1)     ; => error: negative length
```

<a id="api-vector"></a>
#### `vector`

`(vector obj ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Create vector containing the given elements.

**Returns:** A new vector of the arguments; `#()` with no arguments.

```scheme
(vector 1 "a" 'b)    ; => #(1 "a" b)
(vector)             ; => #()
```

<a id="api-vector-length"></a>
#### `vector-length`

`(vector-length vec)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the number of elements in vec.

**Returns:** An exact integer; an error when vec is not a vector.

```scheme
(vector-length (vector 1 2 3))  ; => 3
(vector-length (make-vector 0))  ; => 0
(vector-length '(1))  ; => error: expected vector
```

<a id="api-vector-ref"></a>
#### `vector-ref`

`(vector-ref vec k)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return element at index k (0-based) in vec.

**Returns:** The element at index k; an error when vec is not a vector, k is not a fixnum (flonums are refused), or k is outside 0..length-1.

```scheme
(define v (vector 'a 'b 'c))
(vector-ref v 1)     ; => b
(vector-ref v 3)     ; => error: out of bounds
```

<a id="api-vector-set_21"></a>
#### `vector-set!`

`(vector-set! vec k obj)`

*since 1.0.0*

Set element at index k in vec to obj.

**Returns:** Void; an error when vec is not a vector, k is not a fixnum in 0..length-1, or vec is a quoted literal in the read-only code image.

Quoted literals of an app loaded from the read-only code image (XIP) cannot be modified: mutating one raises "cannot modify a literal constant". Mutate freshly allocated data (list, vector, cons, make-vector) instead.

```scheme
(define v (make-vector 3 0))
(vector-set! v 1 'x)
v                    ; => #(0 x 0)
(vector-set! v 3 'y) ; => error: out of bounds
```

<a id="api-vector-_3elist"></a>
#### `vector->list`

`(vector->list vec)`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert vector elements to a newly allocated list.

**Returns:** A new list of the elements in order; an error when vec is not a vector.

```scheme
(vector->list (vector 1 2 3))  ; => (1 2 3)
(vector->list (vector))  ; => ()
```

<a id="api-list-_3evector"></a>
#### `list->vector`

`(list->vector list)`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert list elements to a newly allocated vector.

**Returns:** A new vector of the elements in order. Not checked: a non-list gives `#()` and the tail of an improper list is dropped.

```scheme
(list->vector '(1 2 3))  ; => #(1 2 3)
(list->vector '())   ; => #()
```

<a id="api-vector-fill_21"></a>
#### `vector-fill!`

`(vector-fill! vec fill)`

*since 1.0.0*

Set all elements of vec to fill.

**Returns:** Void; an error when vec is not a vector or is a quoted literal in the read-only code image.

Quoted literals of an app loaded from the read-only code image (XIP) cannot be modified: mutating one raises "cannot modify a literal constant". Mutate freshly allocated data (list, vector, cons, make-vector) instead.

```scheme
(define v (vector 1 2 3))
(vector-fill! v 0)
v                    ; => #(0 0 0)
```

<a id="api-string_3f"></a>
#### `string?`

`(string? obj)`

*since 1.0.0*

Test if obj is a string.

**Returns:** #t or #f; symbols and characters (integers) are not strings.

```scheme
(string? "abc")      ; => #t
(string? 'abc)       ; => #f
(string? #\a)        ; => #f
```

<a id="api-string-length"></a>
#### `string-length`

`(string-length str)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the length of str in bytes (UTF-8: a non-ASCII character counts 2-4).

**Returns:** An exact integer, the number of bytes; an error when str is not a string.

Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions.

```scheme
(string-length "abc")  ; => 3
(string-length "")   ; => 0
(string-length "été")  ; => 5
```

<a id="api-string-ref"></a>
#### `string-ref`

`(string-ref str k)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the byte at byte index k of str as an integer (a character code).

**Returns:** An integer 0..255 (for ASCII the character code: `(string-ref "abc" 0)` is 97 = `#\a`); an error when str is not a string, k not a fixnum, or k outside 0..length-1.

Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

```scheme
(string-ref "abc" 1)  ; => 98
(= (string-ref "abc" 0) #\a)  ; => #t
(string-ref "abc" 3)  ; => error: out of bounds
```

<a id="api-string-append"></a>
#### `string-append`

`(string-append str ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Concatenate strings into a new string.

**Returns:** A new string; `""` with no arguments; an error when an argument is not a string (convert numbers with `number->string`).

```scheme
(string-append "foo" "bar" "!")  ; => "foobar!"
(string-append "T=" (number->string 21) "C")  ; => "T=21C"
(string-append)      ; => ""
(string-append "a" 1)  ; => error: expected string
```

<a id="api-substring"></a>
#### `substring`

`(substring str start end)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the bytes [start, end) of str as a new string.

**Returns:** A new string of end - start bytes; an error when str is not a string, start or end is not a fixnum (end is required), or not 0 <= start <= end <= length.

Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. Cutting inside a multi-byte character gives invalid UTF-8.

```scheme
(substring "hello" 1 3)  ; => "el"
(substring "hello" 0 0)  ; => ""
(substring "hello" 2 9)  ; => error: invalid slice
```

<a id="api-symbol-_3estring"></a>
#### `symbol->string`

`(symbol->string sym)`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert symbol to string.

**Returns:** A new string of the symbol name; an error when sym is not a symbol.

```scheme
(symbol->string 'abc)  ; => "abc"
(symbol->string "abc")  ; => error: expected symbol
```

<a id="api-string-_3esymbol"></a>
#### `string->symbol`

`(string->symbol str)`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert string to interned symbol.

**Returns:** The interned symbol named str (eq? to the same name written literally); an error when str is not a string.

```scheme
(string->symbol "hello")  ; => hello
(eq? (string->symbol "hello") 'hello)  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-string-_3enumber"></a>
#### `string->number`

`(string->number str [radix])`

*since 1.0.0*

Parse a number from str (radix 10 by default; #x #b #o #d prefixes), or return #f if invalid.

**Returns:** An exact integer (bignum when large), a flonum for decimal notation with "." or an exponent (radix 10 only), or #f when str is not a whole number (no surrounding text, no rationals); an error when str is not a string.

Leading whitespace is accepted only by the flonum parser: `(string->number " 12")` gives 12.0, `"12 "` gives #f.

```scheme
(string->number "42")    ; => 42
(string->number "-3.25") ; => -3.25
(string->number "ff" 16) ; => 255
(string->number "#b101") ; => 5
(string->number "12abc") ; => #f
```

<a id="api-number-_3estring"></a>
#### `number->string`

`(number->string num [radix])`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert number to string; integers in radix (default 10), flonums with up to 6 significant digits.

**Returns:** A new string. Integers are exact in any radix 2..36; flonums use C "%g": 6 significant digits and no ".0" (`2.0` gives "2"). An error when num is not a number.

For a fixed number of decimals, scale and round an integer, or format with `string->fixed` on input.

```scheme
(number->string 42)      ; => "42"
(number->string 255 16)  ; => "ff"
(number->string 3.5)     ; => "3.5"
(number->string (/ 1 3)) ; => "0.333333"
```

<a id="api-list-_3estring"></a>
#### `list->string`

`(list->string chars)`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert a list of byte values (character codes 0..255) to a string.

**Returns:** A new string with one byte per element. Not checked: values are truncated to their low byte, non-integer elements become NUL bytes, and a non-list gives "".

Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

```scheme
(list->string (list 104 105))  ; => "hi"
(list->string (list #\o #\k))  ; => "ok"
(list->string '())   ; => ""
```

<a id="api-string-_3elist"></a>
#### `string->list`

`(string->list str)`

*since 1.0.0*

Convert a string to the list of its bytes (character codes 0..255).

**Returns:** A new list of integers 0..255, one per byte; an error when str is not a string.

Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

```scheme
(string->list "hi")  ; => (104 105)
(string->list "")    ; => ()
(list->string (reverse (string->list "abc")))  ; => "cba"
```

<a id="api-string-_3eints"></a>
#### `string->ints`

`(string->ints str)`

*since 1.0.0*

Integers of a comma-separated string: (string->ints "12,-3,7") => (12 -3 7). Reads the series fields sent by the app proxy.

**Returns:** A list of exact integers, at most 160 of them, bignums past the fixnum range. Spaces around fields are skipped, a field keeps its leading signed digits (up to 15) and fields without digits are dropped; an error when str is not a string.

```scheme
(string->ints "12,-3,7")  ; => (12 -3 7)
(string->ints "1, 2 ,x,3")  ; => (1 2 3)
(string->ints "")    ; => ()
```

<a id="api-string-_3efixed"></a>
#### `string->fixed`

`(string->fixed str [digits])`

*since 1.0.0*

Leading decimal number of str times 10^digits as an integer: (string->fixed "12.3 %" 1) => 123.

**Returns:** An exact integer, rounded half up on the next digit, or #f when str (after leading spaces) does not start with a number; "." or "," separates decimals and trailing text is ignored. digits defaults to 0; an error when str is not a string or digits is outside 0..9. Allocates no flonum.

```scheme
(string->fixed "12.3 %" 1)  ; => 123
(string->fixed "-0,5 V" 2)  ; => -50
(string->fixed "3.145" 2)   ; => 315
(string->fixed "n/a" 1)     ; => #f
```

<a id="api-string_3d_3f"></a>
#### `string=?`

`(string=? s1 s2 s3 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

String equality: all arguments have the same bytes.

**Returns:** #t or #f; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or when an argument is not a string.

```scheme
(string=? "abc" "abc")  ; => #t
(string=? "abc" "ABC")  ; => #f
(string=? "a" "a" "a")  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-string_3c_3f"></a>
#### `string<?`

`(string<? s1 s2 s3 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Lexicographic byte order: each argument is less than the next.

**Returns:** #t or #f, comparing bytes (case-sensitive: "B" < "a"; a proper prefix is less); an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-string.

```scheme
(string<? "apple" "banana")  ; => #t
(string<? "ab" "abc")  ; => #t
(string<? "B" "a")   ; => #t
```

<a id="api-string_3e_3f"></a>
#### `string>?`

`(string>? s1 s2 s3 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Lexicographic byte order: each argument is greater than the next.

**Returns:** #t or #f, comparing bytes as for `string<?`; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-string.

```scheme
(string>? "b" "a")   ; => #t
(string>? "c" "b" "a")  ; => #t
(string>? "a" "a")   ; => #f
```

<a id="api-string-split"></a>
#### `string-split`

`(string-split str sep)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-split)` is `#f`)*

The pieces of str between occurrences of sep.

**Returns:** A list of new strings: the bytes of str between non-overlapping occurrences of sep, scanned from the left. sep is a non-empty string or a character (byte value). Adjacent separators give empty strings; `("")` for "". An error when str is not a string or sep is empty or of another type.

Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions.

```scheme
(string-split "a,b,,c" ",")  ; => ("a" "b" "" "c")
(string-split "k=v" #\=)     ; => ("k" "v")
(string-split "abc" ";")     ; => ("abc")
```

<a id="api-string-join"></a>
#### `string-join`

`(string-join strings [sep])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-join)` is `#f`)*

Concatenate strings with sep between them.

**Returns:** A new string: the elements of the list strings with sep (default " ") between consecutive ones; "" for `()`. An error when strings is not a list of strings or sep is not a string.

```scheme
(string-join '("a" "b" "c") ",")  ; => "a,b,c"
(string-join '("hello" "world"))  ; => "hello world"
(string-join '() ",")  ; => ""
```

<a id="api-string-trim"></a>
#### `string-trim`

`(string-trim str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-trim)` is `#f`)*

str without leading and trailing whitespace.

**Returns:** A new string without the leading and trailing ASCII whitespace bytes (space, tab, LF, CR, VT, FF); other bytes are kept. An error when str is not a string.

```scheme
(string-trim "  42 \r\n")  ; => "42"
(string-trim "a b")  ; => "a b"
(string-trim "   ")  ; => ""
```

<a id="api-string-index"></a>
#### `string-index`

`(string-index str sub [start])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-index)` is `#f`)*

Byte index of the first sub at or after start, or #f.

**Returns:** The byte offset in str of the first occurrence of sub (a string, or a character byte value) that begins at or after start (default 0), or #f; an empty sub gives start. An error when start is not in 0..length or an argument has the wrong type.

Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. The result can be passed to `substring`.

```scheme
(string-index "key=value" "=")  ; => 3
(string-index "a.b.c" #\. 2)    ; => 3
(string-index "abc" "x")        ; => #f
```

<a id="api-string-upcase"></a>
#### `string-upcase`

`(string-upcase str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-upcase)` is `#f`)*

ASCII letters to upper case.

**Returns:** A new string with a-z changed to A-Z; every other byte (including UTF-8 sequences) unchanged. An error when str is not a string.

```scheme
(string-upcase "Hello, world")  ; => "HELLO, WORLD"
(string-upcase "abc123")  ; => "ABC123"
```

<a id="api-string-downcase"></a>
#### `string-downcase`

`(string-downcase str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-downcase)` is `#f`)*

ASCII letters to lower case.

**Returns:** A new string with A-Z changed to a-z; every other byte (including UTF-8 sequences) unchanged. An error when str is not a string.

```scheme
(string-downcase "Hello, World")  ; => "hello, world"
(string=? (string-downcase "OK") "ok")  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-string-prefix_3f"></a>
#### `string-prefix?`

`(string-prefix? prefix str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-prefix?)` is `#f`)*

Whether str starts with prefix.

**Returns:** #t when the first bytes of str equal prefix (always #t for ""), else #f; an error when an argument is not a string.

```scheme
(string-prefix? "temp:" "temp:21.5")  ; => #t
(string-prefix? "abc" "ab")  ; => #f
(string-prefix? "" "x")  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-string-suffix_3f"></a>
#### `string-suffix?`

`(string-suffix? suffix str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-suffix?)` is `#f`)*

Whether str ends with suffix.

**Returns:** #t when the last bytes of str equal suffix (always #t for ""), else #f; an error when an argument is not a string.

```scheme
(string-suffix? ".scm" "main.scm")  ; => #t
(string-suffix? ".scm" "scm")  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-string-pad-left"></a>
#### `string-pad-left`

`(string-pad-left str n [char])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'string-pad-left)` is `#f`)*

str padded on the left to n characters.

**Returns:** A new string of exactly n bytes: str preceded by copies of char (a byte value, default #\space) when shorter, or its last n bytes when longer. An error when n is not a non-negative fixnum or char is not 0..255.

Strings are UTF-8 byte strings: lengths and indexes count bytes, and the elements are byte values 0..255, so a non-ASCII character spans several positions. Meant for ASCII text such as clock digits.

```scheme
(string-pad-left "7" 2 #\0)    ; => "07"
(string-pad-left "42" 5)       ; => "   42"
(string-pad-left "12345" 3)    ; => "345"
```

<a id="component-char"></a>
### Characters (`char`)

Characters and their codes.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(char->integer char)`](#api-char-_3einteger) | stable |
| [`(integer->char k)`](#api-integer-_3echar) | stable |
| [`(char=? c1 c2 c3 ...)`](#api-char_3d_3f) | stable |
| [`(char<? c1 c2 c3 ...)`](#api-char_3c_3f) | stable |
| [`(char>? c1 c2 c3 ...)`](#api-char_3e_3f) | stable |
| [`(char<=? c1 c2 c3 ...)`](#api-char_3c_3d_3f) | stable |
| [`(char>=? c1 c2 c3 ...)`](#api-char_3e_3d_3f) | stable |

<a id="api-char-_3einteger"></a>
#### `char->integer`

`(char->integer char)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the code of char; characters are already integers, so this is the identity.

**Returns:** The integer itself (`#\A` is 65); an error when char is not a fixnum.

MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

```scheme
(char->integer #\A)  ; => 65
(char->integer #\space)  ; => 32
(char->integer "a")  ; => error: expected fixnum/char
```

<a id="api-integer-_3echar"></a>
#### `integer->char`

`(integer->char k)`

*since 1.0.0*

Return the character with code k; characters are integers, so this is the identity.

**Returns:** k itself (written as an integer); an error when k is not a fixnum.

MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

```scheme
(integer->char 65)   ; => 65
(= (integer->char 97) #\a)  ; => #t
(list->string (list (integer->char 72) (integer->char 105)))  ; => "Hi"
```

<a id="api-char_3d_3f"></a>
#### `char=?`

`(char=? c1 c2 c3 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Character equality: all codes are equal.

**Returns:** #t or #f; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or when an argument is not a fixnum (character).

MiniScheme has no separate character type: a character is its integer code. `#\a` reads as 97, and `write` prints characters as integers.

```scheme
(char=? #\a #\a)     ; => #t
(char=? #\a #\A)     ; => #f
(char=? (string-ref "x" 0) #\x)  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-char_3c_3f"></a>
#### `char<?`

`(char<? c1 c2 c3 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Character order: each code is less than the next.

**Returns:** #t or #f by code; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-fixnum.

```scheme
(char<? #\a #\b #\c)  ; => #t
(char<? #\b #\a)     ; => #f
(char<? #\a)         ; => error: expected 2 arguments
```

<a id="api-char_3e_3f"></a>
#### `char>?`

`(char>? c1 c2 c3 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Character order: each code is greater than the next.

**Returns:** #t or #f by code; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-fixnum.

```scheme
(char>? #\b #\a)     ; => #t
(char>? #\a #\a)     ; => #f
```

<a id="api-char_3c_3d_3f"></a>
#### `char<=?`

`(char<=? c1 c2 c3 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Character order: each code is less than or equal to the next.

**Returns:** #t or #f by code; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-fixnum.

```scheme
(define c (string-ref "7" 0))
(and (char<=? #\0 c) (char<=? c #\9))  ; => #t
(char<=? #\b #\a)    ; => #f
```

<a id="api-char_3e_3d_3f"></a>
#### `char>=?`

`(char>=? c1 c2 c3 ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Character order: each code is greater than or equal to the next.

**Returns:** #t or #f by code; an error with fewer than 2 arguments or a non-fixnum.

```scheme
(char>=? #\b #\a #\a)  ; => #t
(char>=? #\a #\b)    ; => #f
```
