<a id="api-display-model"></a>
#### `display-model`

`(display-model)`

*since 1.0.0*

Panel model string.

**Returns:** String, "ILI9488-8BIT-PARALLEL-480x320" on every build.

```scheme
(display-model)  ; => "ILI9488-8BIT-PARALLEL-480x320"
```

<a id="api-display-rotation"></a>
#### `display-rotation`

`(display-rotation [r])`

*since 1.0.0 · older names: `gui-rotation`*

Panel rotation 0..3 (0 and 2 portrait 320x480, 1 and 3 landscape 480x320); returns the rotation.

**Returns:** Fixnum 0..3, the rotation after the call (r is taken modulo 4). Setting it re-initializes the screen in direct mode with the new size and clears it. A non-integer r is ignored.

The WASM simulator and the PC build keep a simulated rotation. Setting a rotation goes through `gui-init`, so the buffer mode becomes `direct` (see `gui-mode`) until the next boot; call `gui-invalidate` to have the app redrawn.

```scheme
(display-rotation)            ; => 0
(display-rotation 1)          ; => 1
(list (gui-width) (gui-height))  ; => (480 320)
(display-rotation 0)          ; => 0
```

<a id="api-display-dma-ram"></a>
#### `display-dma-ram`

`(display-dma-ram)`

*since 1.0.0 · older names: `lcd-dma-ram`*

Bytes of the LCD driver's DMA and staging buffers (0 without DMA).

**Returns:** Fixnum >= 0: the bytes on the board; always 0 in the WASM simulator and on the PC.

```scheme
(>= (display-dma-ram) 0)  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-gui-init"></a>
#### `gui-init`

`(gui-init [w h])`

*since 1.0.0*

Re-initialize the screen as w x h pixels (default 320x480) in direct mode and clear it.

**Returns:** Void. Without two integers the default size is used; a size over 480x480 pixels keeps the current size.

Legacy: the firmware sets the screen up at boot from config.ini [display] (mode, band_lines, color_bits). `gui-init` always switches to direct mode; to change the size only use `gui-set-resolution`.

```scheme
(gui-init 480 320)
(list (gui-width) (gui-height) (gui-mode))  ; => (480 320 direct)
```

<a id="api-gui-clear"></a>
#### `gui-clear`

`(gui-clear [color])`

*since 1.0.0*

Fill the current clip (the whole screen without one) with an RGB565 color (default dark slate 2179).

**Returns:** Void.

In `gui-render-proc` the clip is the span being redrawn, which the runtime has already cleared to 2179 (#0b1118). Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-clear (gui-rgb 0 0 64))
(gui-pixel 100 200)  ; => 8
```

<a id="api-gui-flush"></a>
#### `gui-flush`

`(gui-flush)`

*since 1.0.0*

Mark the whole screen changed for the host canvas (simulator). The board sends pixels by itself.

**Returns:** Void.

Legacy. Apps redraw through `gui-invalidate` and `gui-render-proc`; in full mode `gui-flush-dirty` sends rows drawn outside a render at once.

```scheme
(gui-flush-dirty)
(gui-flush)
(gui-dirty-rect)  ; => (0 0 320 480)
```

<a id="api-gui-pixel"></a>
#### `gui-pixel`

`(gui-pixel x y [color])`

*since 1.0.0*

Set one pixel to an RGB565 color; (gui-pixel x y) reads the stored color back.

**Returns:** Void when setting; with two arguments the RGB565 fixnum at x y (0 outside the screen or where no pixels are kept: band rows not being drawn, direct mode). Pixels outside the clip are skipped.

At color bits below 16 the read-back is the palette color the pixel was mapped to. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-pixel 10 20 (gui-rgb 255 0 0))
(gui-pixel 10 20)  ; => 63488
```

<a id="api-gui-line"></a>
#### `gui-line`

`(gui-line x0 y0 x1 y1 color)`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw a one-pixel line between two points, both ends included.

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless all five arguments are integers.

Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-line 0 0 99 99 (gui-rgb 0 255 0))
(gui-pixel 50 50)  ; => 2016
```

<a id="api-gui-rect"></a>
#### `gui-rect`

`(gui-rect x y w h color [filled])`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw a rectangle, filled unless filled is #f (then a one-pixel outline).

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless x y w h color are integers or when w or h <= 0.

Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-rect 10 10 100 40 (gui-rgb 0 0 255))
(gui-rect 10 60 100 40 (gui-rgb 255 255 255) #f)
(list (gui-pixel 50 30) (gui-pixel 50 80) (gui-pixel 50 60))  ; => (31 2179 65535)
```

<a id="api-gui-round-rect"></a>
#### `gui-round-rect`

`(gui-round-rect x y w h r color [filled])`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw a rectangle with corners of radius r, filled unless filled is #f.

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless the first six arguments are integers. r is limited to half the width and height; r <= 0 draws a plain rectangle.

Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-round-rect 10 10 120 40 8 (gui-rgb 255 128 0))
(list (gui-pixel 10 10) (gui-pixel 70 30))  ; => (2179 64512)
```

<a id="api-gui-circle"></a>
#### `gui-circle`

`(gui-circle cx cy r color [filled])`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw a circle of radius r around cx cy, filled unless filled is #f.

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless the first four arguments are integers. r <= 0 draws the center pixel.

Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-circle 160 240 30 (gui-rgb 255 0 0))
(gui-circle 160 240 50 (gui-rgb 255 255 255) #f)
(list (gui-pixel 160 240) (gui-pixel 210 240))  ; => (63488 65535)
```

<a id="api-gui-text"></a>
#### `gui-text`

`(gui-text x y str color [size])`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw UTF-8 text with its top-left corner at x y in the current font; size 2.. draws the built-in 8x8 font scaled.

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless x y are integers, str a string and color an integer.

size 1 (default) is `gui-text-styled` with the current font (`gui-set-font`). Larger sizes scale the built-in 8x8 ASCII glyphs and 16x16 CJK glyphs by size; a "\n" starts a new line. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-text 10 10 "Hello" (gui-rgb 255 255 255))
(gui-text 10 40 "BIG" (gui-rgb 255 255 0) 3)
```

<a id="api-gui-set-font"></a>
#### `gui-set-font`

`(gui-set-font font-id)`

*since 1.0.0*

Set the current font: 0 system 16 px, 1 clock 32 px (digits), 2..7 registered or loaded fonts.

**Returns:** Void. Any integer is kept; text in an id without a font uses the system font.

The current font is global (shared by every app until changed) and used by `gui-text`, `gui-text-width` and the text procedures whose font argument is left out.

```scheme
(gui-set-font 1)
(gui-get-font)  ; => 1
(gui-set-font 0)
```

<a id="api-gui-get-font"></a>
#### `gui-get-font`

`(gui-get-font)`

*since 1.0.0*

The current font id (see gui-set-font).

**Returns:** Fixnum, the id last given to `gui-set-font` (0 at boot).

```scheme
(gui-get-font)  ; => 0
```

<a id="api-gui-text-width"></a>
#### `gui-text-width`

`(gui-text-width str [font-id])`

*since 1.0.0*

Width in pixels of str drawn in a font (default the current font).

**Returns:** Fixnum >= 0, the sum of the glyph advances; 0 when str is not a string.

Lay out text with it: right-align at xr with `(gui-text-styled (- xr (gui-text-width s f)) y s c f)`. A missing glyph counts as the width it is drawn with (the system font, or a box).

```scheme
(gui-text-width "Hello" 0)  ; => 40
(gui-text-width "12:30" 1)  ; => 92
```

<a id="api-gui-text-styled"></a>
#### `gui-text-styled`

`(gui-text-styled x y str color [font-id])`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw UTF-8 text with its top-left corner at x y in a font (default the current font).

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless x y are integers, str a string and color an integer.

Glyphs the font lacks come from the system font, then the built-in font; with none a box is drawn. "\n" starts a new line (font height + 2 lower). Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-text-styled 10 10 "Temperature" (gui-rgb 200 200 200) 0)
(gui-text-styled 10 30 "21:45" (gui-rgb 255 255 255) 1)
```

<a id="api-gui-text-box"></a>
#### `gui-text-box`

`(gui-text-box x y w h str color [font-id [halign [valign]]])`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw one line of text aligned in a box and clipped to it. halign 0 left, 1 center, 2 right; valign 0 top, 1 middle, 2 bottom.

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless x y w h are integers, str a string and color an integer. font-id defaults to the current font, halign and valign to 0.

Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-rect 0 0 320 40 (gui-rgb 24 28 43))
(gui-text-box 0 0 320 40 "Weather" (gui-rgb 255 255 255) 0 1 1)
```

<a id="api-gui-text-scaled"></a>
#### `gui-text-scaled`

`(gui-text-scaled x y str color scale [font-id])`

*since 1.7.0*

Draw UTF-8 text in a font (default the current one) with every dot scale x scale (2..8): large text without a large font.

**Returns:** Void. scale 1 or less draws as gui-text-styled, more than 8 as 8. An error when x, y, color or scale is not an integer or str is not a string.

The glyphs of the font chain (the system font, its fallbacks) are enlarged: a dot set (an anti-aliased dot more than half covered) becomes a scale x scale square, so the edges are blocky but no font file is needed. Lines (\n) are (height + 2) x scale apart. Check it with (defined? 'gui-text-scaled) on older firmware. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-text-scaled 10 40 "阿莫西林" (gui-rgb 255 255 255) 2)   ; 16 px font -> 32 px
(gui-text-scaled 10 40 'name 0 2)  ; => error: expected
```

<a id="api-gui-chart"></a>
#### `gui-chart`

`(gui-chart x y w h ring start count lo hi color)`

*since 1.0.0*

Line chart of count values of the vector ring from index start (wrapping), scaled from lo..hi to the box.

**Returns:** Void. An error when ring is not a vector or another argument is not an integer; nothing is drawn when count < 2 or hi <= lo.

Values are clamped to lo..hi; elements that are not integers count as lo. count is limited to the vector length and 320 points, h to 256. Points are spread evenly over w. A ring buffer of samples draws in order with start = the oldest index. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(define temps (vector 18 19 21 24 23 20))
(gui-chart 10 300 300 100 temps 0 6 15 25 (gui-rgb 0 200 255))
(gui-chart 10 300 300 100 '(1 2) 0 2 0 9 0)  ; => error: expected
```

<a id="api-gui-image"></a>
#### `gui-image`

`(gui-image x y path [frame [speed]])`

*since 1.5.0*

Draw an image file at x y (its top-left corner): a baseline JPEG, or an animation (a MANI file of JPEG frames, which the photo album's web page makes from a GIF).

**Returns:** Void. frame: #t (the default) plays an animation by its frame delays, #f shows its first frame, a number that frame; speed: percent of the delays' pace, 10..1000 (100). path is in the app's folder like the fs- procedures. Errors: a file that cannot be opened or is not a baseline JPEG / MANI file (progressive JPEG, PNG and GIF need converting: the album's page does it in the browser).

One display-list command: a band decodes only the JPEG's MCU rows it covers (the decoder remembers where each one starts), so a full-screen photo needs no frame buffer; about 6 KB while an image is open. A playing animation redraws only its own box at its shortest frame delay, its clock starting when it appears. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-image 0 0 "photos/none.jpg")  ; => error: gui-image: cannot open the image file
```

<a id="api-image-info"></a>
#### `image-info`

`(image-info path)`

*since 1.5.0*

The size of an image file and its frames: (width height frames total-ms).

**Returns:** The list, or #f when the file is missing or not an image gui-image can draw. total-ms is an animation's length (0 for one frame).

Center an image: x = (320 - width) / 2. Opening an image reads only its headers.

```scheme
(image-info "photos/none.jpg")  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-gui-bitmap"></a>
#### `gui-bitmap`

`(gui-bitmap x y w h data scale fg [bg])`

*since 1.4.0*

Draw a 1-bit bitmap of w x h dots, each dot scale x scale pixels: set dots in fg, clear ones in bg (left as they are without bg).

**Returns:** Void. data is a string of bytes: h rows of (w + 7) / 8 bytes each, the first dot of a byte its high bit (a row ends on a byte boundary). Errors: data shorter than that, w or h not 1..4096, scale not 1..255, another argument not an integer.

One display-list command however many dots (the rows go to its string pool): a QR code or an icon costs what one rectangle does, where gui-rect per dot or per run used up the 512-command list. A band draws only its rows, each row's runs of set dots as single rectangles. Build data with list->string of (integer->char byte) values; it may hold 0 bytes. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
;; a 2 x 2 checker: rows #b10000000 and #b01000000, 10 px dots
(define checker (list->string (list (integer->char 128) (integer->char 64))))
(gui-bitmap 100 100 2 2 checker 10 (gui-rgb 255 255 255) 0)
(gui-pixel 105 105)  ; => 65535
(gui-pixel 115 105)  ; => 0
(gui-pixel 115 115)  ; => 65535
(gui-bitmap 0 0 16 2 checker 1 0)  ; => error: data has
```

<a id="api-gui-arc"></a>
#### `gui-arc`

`(gui-arc cx cy r thickness start-deg sweep-deg color)`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw a ring arc of outer radius r: 0 degrees is 3 o'clock, sweeping clockwise.

**Returns:** Void. An error when an argument is not an integer; nothing is drawn when r, thickness or sweep-deg <= 0. sweep-deg >= 360 draws the full ring.

A gauge: `(gui-arc cx cy r 8 135 (quotient (* 270 pct) 100) color)` over a dim full 270-degree track. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-arc 160 240 50 8 270 90 (gui-rgb 0 255 0))
(gui-pixel 192 208)  ; => 2016
(gui-arc 160 240 50 8 0 90)  ; => error: expected
```

<a id="api-gui-push-clip"></a>
#### `gui-push-clip`

`(gui-push-clip x y w h)`

*since 1.0.0*

Save the current clip and clip drawing to the rectangle x y w h (no allocation).

**Returns:** Void. An error when an argument is not an integer or when pushes nest deeper than 8.

Pair every push with a `gui-pop-clip`. The stack is reset each time the runtime calls `gui-render-proc`. Inside a render the effective clip is also limited to the rows being redrawn.

```scheme
(gui-push-clip 0 0 100 50)
(gui-get-clip)  ; => (0 0 100 50)
(gui-pop-clip)
(gui-get-clip)  ; => (0 0 320 480)
```

<a id="api-gui-pop-clip"></a>
#### `gui-pop-clip`

`(gui-pop-clip)`

*since 1.0.0*

Restore the clip saved by the matching gui-push-clip.

**Returns:** Void. An error when no clip is saved.

```scheme
(gui-push-clip 20 20 80 80)
(gui-rect 0 0 320 480 (gui-rgb 255 0 0))
(gui-pop-clip)
(list (gui-pixel 10 10) (gui-pixel 50 50))  ; => (2179 63488)
(gui-pop-clip)  ; => error: no saved clip
```

<a id="api-gui-mode"></a>
#### `gui-mode`

`(gui-mode)`

*since 1.0.0*

Buffer mode: band (a few rows at a time), full (whole frame) or direct (no buffer).

**Returns:** Symbol band, full or direct. Set by config.ini [display] mode; full falls back to band, band to direct, when RAM is short.

```scheme
(gui-mode)  ; => full
```

<a id="api-gui-color-bits"></a>
#### `gui-color-bits`

`(gui-color-bits [n])`

*since 1.0.0*

Bits per stored pixel: 16 (RGB565) or 8, 4, 2, 1 (palette indices); setting it redraws.

**Returns:** Fixnum, the bits after the call. An error when n is not 16, 8, 4, 2 or 1.

Fewer bits cost less buffer RAM (bits/16 of the RGB565 size); colors are mapped to the palette of the color scheme (`gui-color-scheme`). Changing it re-creates the buffer, clears the screen and queues a full redraw. Kept until the next boot (config.ini [display] color_bits sets the boot value).

```scheme
(gui-color-bits)     ; => 16
(gui-color-bits 4)   ; => 4
(gui-buffer-ram)     ; => 76800
(gui-color-bits 16)  ; => 16
(gui-color-bits 3)   ; => error: expected 16, 8, 4, 2 or 1
```

<a id="api-gui-color-scheme"></a>
#### `gui-color-scheme`

`(gui-color-scheme [name])`

*since 1.0.0*

Color scheme: color, gray, eink, green, amber, cyan, gameboy, invert (RGB negative) or custom.

**Returns:** Symbol, the scheme after the call. name is a symbol or string; older names (mono, e-ink, matrix, negative, ...) are accepted. An error for an unknown name.

Ramp schemes (gray ... gameboy) map colors by brightness; at 16 bits they tint the screen with 64 levels. Setting a scheme queues a full redraw; it is kept until the next boot (config.ini [display] palette).

```scheme
(gui-color-scheme)          ; => color
(gui-color-scheme 'amber)   ; => amber
(gui-color-scheme "color")  ; => color
(gui-color-scheme 'sepia)   ; => error: unknown scheme
```

<a id="api-gui-buffer-ram"></a>
#### `gui-buffer-ram`

`(gui-buffer-ram)`

*since 1.0.0*

Bytes held by the band or frame buffer (0 in direct mode).

**Returns:** Fixnum: width x rows x bits / 8 (the band rows in band mode, the screen in full mode).

```scheme
(gui-buffer-ram)  ; => 307200
```

<a id="api-gui-card"></a>
#### `gui-card`

`(gui-card x y w h r bg-color border-color)`

*since 1.0.0*

Rounded card: a filled background plus a one-pixel outline (border 0 or bg-color: none).

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless all seven arguments are integers. r 0 draws square corners.

Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-card 10 10 300 80 8 (gui-rgb 24 28 43) (gui-rgb 41 48 74))
(list (gui-pixel 160 50) (gui-pixel 160 10))  ; => (6373 10633)
```

<a id="api-gui-text-wrap"></a>
#### `gui-text-wrap`

`(gui-text-wrap x y w h str color [font [line-height]])`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw text wrapped to width w, as many lines as fit in h; cut text ends with an ellipsis. Returns the lines drawn.

**Returns:** Fixnum, the number of lines drawn (at least 1 line is drawn when h is smaller than a line). An error when x y w h color are not integers or str is not a string.

Lines break at spaces, or between two characters when either is CJK (Latin words and numbers stay whole; closing punctuation never starts a line); "\n" forces a break. line-height defaults to the font height + 2. Use `gui-text-area` to scroll text that does not fit instead. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(gui-text-wrap 10 10 100 200 "one two three four five six" 65535 0)  ; => 3
(gui-text-wrap 10 10 100 18 "one two three four five six" 65535 0)   ; => 1
```

<a id="api-gui-text-fit"></a>
#### `gui-text-fit`

`(gui-text-fit x y w str color [font])`

*since 1.0.0*

One line of text in a box w pixels wide; a longer line is cut with an ellipsis or scrolls as set by config.ini [text] marquee.

**Returns:** Void. An error when x y w color are not integers or str is not a string.

The box is the font height + 2 tall. Modes (`gui-marquee`): none cuts the line with an ellipsis; pixel and char move it marquee_step pixels or characters marquee_fps times a second; page shows box-wide pieces in turn. Draw it from `gui-render-proc` every time: the runtime animates the box by redrawing only its rows (or its rectangle) without another `gui-invalidate`.

```scheme
(gui-text-fit 10 10 120 "Short" 65535 0)
(gui-text-fit 10 30 120 "A headline much too long for its box" 65535 0)
```

<a id="api-gui-text-area"></a>
#### `gui-text-area`

`(gui-text-area x y w h str color [font [line-h]])`

*since 1.0.0*

Text wrapped to a box; text taller than the box is cut with an ellipsis or scrolls as set by config.ini [text] wrap_marquee.

**Returns:** Void. An error when x y w h color are not integers or str is not a string.

Wraps like `gui-text-wrap`; line-h defaults to the font height + 2. Modes (`gui-marquee 'wrap`): none cuts the text with an ellipsis; pixel rolls it up; line moves wrap_marquee_step lines at a time; page shows the next box-full; wrap_marquee_fps times a second. Draw it from `gui-render-proc`; the box animates by itself.

```scheme
(gui-text-area 10 10 300 60 "A long news summary that needs several lines to fit in this box." 65535 0)
```

<a id="api-gui-marquee"></a>
#### `gui-marquee`

`(gui-marquee ['wrap] [mode [fps [step [hold]]]])`

*since 1.0.0*

Marquee settings (mode fps step hold) of one-line text, or of wrapped text with 'wrap; arguments set them until the next boot.

**Returns:** List (mode fps step hold): mode a symbol, fps a number (0.1..25 refreshes a second), step a fixnum 1..64 (pixels, characters or lines), hold the seconds (0..10) the start stays. An error for a mode the kind does not take.

One-line text (`gui-text-fit`) takes none, pixel, char or page; wrapped text (`gui-text-area`) none, pixel, line or page. Arguments left out keep their values. The boot values come from config.ini [text] (marquee, marquee_fps, marquee_step, marquee_hold and the wrap_ ones); setting them queues a full redraw.

```scheme
(define saved (gui-marquee))
(gui-marquee 'char 2 1 0.5)  ; => (char 2 1 0.5)
(gui-marquee 'wrap)          ; => (line 0.5 1 1)
(gui-marquee 'line)          ; => error: one-line text takes
(apply gui-marquee saved)
```

<a id="api-gui-text-scroll"></a>
#### `gui-text-scroll`

`(gui-text-scroll x y w h str color [font [speed [direction]]])`

*since 1.0.0*

Text longer than its box scrolls in a loop: direction 'left (marquee, default) or 'up (wrapped lines); speed in pixels per second (default 30).

**Returns:** Void. An error when x y w h color are not integers or str is not a string. speed is limited to 0..2000.

Text that fits is drawn still. Draw it from `gui-render-proc` like other text; the offset comes from the frame clock and the runtime redraws only the box while it moves (up to 25 times a second), without running the render procedure again until the app calls `gui-invalidate`.

```scheme
(define (render)
  (gui-text-scroll 10 10 200 20 "Breaking news: a very long headline scrolls" 65535 0 40))
(define gui-render-proc render)
(gui-invalidate)
```

<a id="api-gui-seg7"></a>
#### `gui-seg7`

`(gui-seg7 x y digit-w digit-h thickness str on off glow highlight)`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw seven-segment digits (0-9, -, : and .); unlit segments in off, lit ones in on with optional glow and highlight colors.

**Returns:** Fixnum, the width drawn (as `gui-seg7-width`); 0 and nothing drawn when an argument has the wrong type.

glow != on draws a halo around lit segments; highlight != on (thickness >= 5) a thin bright core. Pass on for both to draw plain segments. Characters other than the digits, "-", ":" and "." leave a blank digit. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(define on (gui-rgb 255 80 0))
(define off (gui-rgb 40 20 10))
(gui-seg7 10 10 30 56 6 "12:45" on off on on)  ; => 152
```

<a id="api-gui-seg7-width"></a>
#### `gui-seg7-width`

`(gui-seg7-width digit-w thickness str)`

*since 1.0.0*

Width in pixels gui-seg7 draws for str.

**Returns:** Fixnum: digit-w per character, thickness + 2 per ":" or ".", plus thickness / 2 + 3 between characters; 0 for wrong arguments.

```scheme
(gui-seg7-width 30 6 "12:45")  ; => 152
(gui-seg7-width 30 6 "")       ; => 0
```

<a id="api-gui-set-resolution"></a>
#### `gui-set-resolution`

`(gui-set-resolution w h)`

*since 1.0.0*

Change the logical screen size, keeping the buffer mode; the screen is cleared and redrawn.

**Returns:** Void. Ignored when w or h <= 0 or w x h is over 480x480 pixels.

It does not rotate the panel: use `display-rotation` for that. In band mode a wider screen gets fewer band rows so the band keeps its RAM.

```scheme
(gui-set-resolution 480 320)
(list (gui-width) (gui-height) (gui-mode))  ; => (480 320 full)
```

<a id="api-gui-set-clip"></a>
#### `gui-set-clip`

`(gui-set-clip x y w h)`

*since 1.0.0*

Clip drawing to a rectangle (limited to the screen).

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless all four arguments are integers. w or h <= 0 clips everything away.

Prefer `gui-push-clip` / `gui-pop-clip`, which restore the caller's clip.

```scheme
(gui-set-clip 0 0 100 50)
(gui-rect 0 0 320 480 (gui-rgb 255 0 0))
(list (gui-pixel 50 25) (gui-pixel 150 25))  ; => (63488 2179)
(gui-reset-clip)
```

<a id="api-gui-reset-clip"></a>
#### `gui-reset-clip`

`(gui-reset-clip)`

*since 1.0.0*

Remove the clip rectangle: drawing reaches the whole screen again.

**Returns:** Void.

```scheme
(gui-set-clip 10 10 50 50)
(gui-reset-clip)
(gui-get-clip)  ; => (0 0 320 480)
```

<a id="api-gui-get-clip"></a>
#### `gui-get-clip`

`(gui-get-clip)`

*since 1.0.0*

Current clip rectangle as (x y w h).

**Returns:** List of four fixnums; (0 0 width height) without a clip.

```scheme
(gui-get-clip)  ; => (0 0 320 480)
(gui-set-clip -10 400 50 200)
(gui-get-clip)  ; => (0 400 40 80)
```

<a id="api-gui-dirty-rect"></a>
#### `gui-dirty-rect`

`(gui-dirty-rect)`

*since 1.0.0*

Bounding box of the screen area changed since the host canvas last took it, as (x y w h).

**Returns:** List of four fixnums; (0 0 0 0) when nothing changed.

For hosts that paint a canvas (the WASM simulator); apps do not need it.

```scheme
(gui-flush-dirty)
(gui-dirty-rect)  ; => (0 0 0 0)
(gui-mark-dirty 10 20 30 40)
(gui-dirty-rect)  ; => (10 20 30 40)
```

<a id="api-gui-mark-dirty"></a>
#### `gui-mark-dirty`

`(gui-mark-dirty x y w h)`

*since 1.0.0*

Mark a rectangle as changed for the host canvas.

**Returns:** Void; ignored unless all four arguments are integers.

It does not redraw anything: to have the app redraw use `gui-invalidate`.

```scheme
(gui-flush-dirty)
(gui-mark-dirty 0 0 40 40)
(gui-dirty-rect-count)  ; => 1
```

<a id="api-gui-dirty-rect-count"></a>
#### `gui-dirty-rect-count`

`(gui-dirty-rect-count)`

*since 1.0.0*

Number of dirty rectangles after merging (at most 8).

**Returns:** Fixnum 0..8.

```scheme
(gui-flush-dirty)
(gui-mark-dirty 0 0 40 40)
(gui-mark-dirty 200 300 40 40)
(gui-dirty-rect-count)  ; => 2
```

<a id="api-gui-dirty-rects"></a>
#### `gui-dirty-rects`

`(gui-dirty-rects)`

*since 1.0.0*

Dirty rectangles after merging into 32-pixel tiles, as a list of (x y w h).

**Returns:** List of up to 8 lists (x y w h), top to bottom; () when nothing changed.

```scheme
(gui-flush-dirty)
(gui-mark-dirty 0 0 40 40)
(gui-mark-dirty 200 300 40 40)
(gui-dirty-rects)  ; => ((0 0 64 64) (192 288 48 52))
```

<a id="api-gui-flush-dirty"></a>
#### `gui-flush-dirty`

`(gui-flush-dirty)`

*since 1.0.0*

Full mode: send the rows drawn outside a render to the panel now.

**Returns:** Void. On the PC build it also clears the dirty rectangles.

The runtime sends such rows at its next display service anyway; call it when the app draws outside `gui-render-proc` and must show the result before a long computation. Other modes: no effect on the panel.

```scheme
(gui-rect 0 0 320 40 (gui-rgb 0 0 128))
(gui-flush-dirty)
```

<a id="api-gui-render-bands"></a>
#### `gui-render-bands`

`(gui-render-bands band-h proc)`

*since 1.0.0*

Call proc once per slice of band-h rows, drawing clipped to the slice: (lambda (i y h) ...) or (lambda (i) ...).

**Returns:** #t; void when band-h is not an integer (nothing is called).

Legacy immediate rendering: in band mode each slice is sent to the panel after proc returns, in full mode the frame after the last slice. band-h is limited to the band rows in band mode. Called from `gui-render-proc` it cannot be recorded, so the render procedure then runs once per band; prefer `gui-render-proc` with `gui-visible?`.

```scheme
(define n 0)
(gui-render-bands 160 (lambda (i y h) (set! n (+ n 1))))  ; => #t
n  ; => 3
```

<a id="api-gui-create-buffer"></a>
#### `gui-create-buffer`

`(gui-create-buffer w h)`

*since 1.0.0*

Create an offscreen RGB565 buffer of w x h pixels; returns its id.

**Returns:** Fixnum id 1..15; -1 when w or h is not a positive integer, memory is short or all 15 buffers are in use.

The buffer holds w x h x 2 bytes of C heap (not the VM heap) until `gui-destroy-buffer`; it starts black.

```scheme
(define buf (gui-create-buffer 64 64))
(> buf 0)  ; => #t
(gui-destroy-buffer buf)
```

<a id="api-gui-destroy-buffer"></a>
#### `gui-destroy-buffer`

`(gui-destroy-buffer id)`

*since 1.0.0*

Free an offscreen buffer (drawing returns to the screen if it was the target).

**Returns:** Void; an unknown id is ignored.

```scheme
(define buf (gui-create-buffer 32 32))
(gui-destroy-buffer buf)
(gui-destroy-buffer buf)
```

<a id="api-gui-set-target"></a>
#### `gui-set-target`

`(gui-set-target id)`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw into offscreen buffer id (0 = the screen); the clip becomes the whole target.

**Returns:** Void; an unknown id is ignored.

Ignored while `gui-render-proc` is being recorded (band mode then runs the render procedure once per band). Prepare buffers outside the render procedure.

```scheme
(define buf (gui-create-buffer 40 40))
(gui-set-target buf)
(gui-circle 20 20 15 (gui-rgb 255 0 0))
(gui-pixel 20 20)  ; => 63488
(gui-set-target 0)
(gui-destroy-buffer buf)
```

<a id="api-gui-reset-target"></a>
#### `gui-reset-target`

`(gui-reset-target)`

*since 1.0.0*

Draw to the screen again (same as (gui-set-target 0)).

**Returns:** Void.

```scheme
(define buf (gui-create-buffer 40 40))
(gui-set-target buf)
(gui-reset-target)
(gui-get-clip)  ; => (0 0 320 480)
(gui-destroy-buffer buf)
```

<a id="api-gui-blit-buffer"></a>
#### `gui-blit-buffer`

`(gui-blit-buffer x y id)`

*since 1.0.0*

Copy an offscreen buffer to the current target at x y (clipped).

**Returns:** Void; an unknown id is ignored.

Cannot be recorded: called from `gui-render-proc` in band mode, the render procedure runs once per band. Draw from `gui-render-proc`: the runtime calls it for the rows queued by `gui-invalidate` (in band mode it runs once, recorded as a display list that is replayed for each band, and the drawing is clipped to the rows being redrawn). Outside it, full mode keeps the pixels and sends them to the panel at the next display service, direct mode draws straight to the panel, and band mode loses them when the next band is drawn.

```scheme
(define buf (gui-create-buffer 40 40))
(gui-set-target buf)
(gui-clear (gui-rgb 0 255 0))
(gui-reset-target)
(gui-blit-buffer 100 100 buf)
(gui-pixel 120 120)  ; => 2016
(gui-destroy-buffer buf)
```

<a id="api-gui-framebuffer-enable"></a>
#### `gui-framebuffer-enable`

`(gui-framebuffer-enable on?)`

*since 1.0.0*

Switch to full mode (true) or direct mode (#f); returns whether full mode is on.

**Returns:** #t in full mode after the call, else #f (full mode needs RAM for the frame: without it the mode becomes band).

Switching re-creates the buffer, clears the screen and queues a full redraw.

```scheme
(gui-framebuffer-enable #f)  ; => #f
(gui-mode)                   ; => direct
(gui-framebuffer-enable #t)  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-gui-framebuffer-enabled_3f"></a>
#### `gui-framebuffer-enabled?`

`(gui-framebuffer-enabled?)`

*since 1.0.0*

True in full (frame buffer) mode.

**Returns:** #t in full mode, #f in band or direct mode.

```scheme
(gui-framebuffer-enabled?)  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-gui-framebuffer-ram"></a>
#### `gui-framebuffer-ram`

`(gui-framebuffer-ram)`

*since 1.0.0*

Bytes held by the band or frame buffer (same as gui-buffer-ram).

**Returns:** Fixnum, 0 in direct mode.

```scheme
(gui-framebuffer-ram)  ; => 307200
```

<a id="api-gui-color-depth"></a>
#### `gui-color-depth`

`(gui-color-depth [bits])`

*since 1.0.0*

Legacy gui-color-bits: bits per stored pixel; a value other than 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 is ignored.

**Returns:** Fixnum, the bits per pixel after the call. Never an error.

```scheme
(gui-color-depth)    ; => 16
(gui-color-depth 3)  ; => 16
```

<a id="api-gui-color-format"></a>
#### `gui-color-format`

`(gui-color-format)`

*since 1.0.0*

Panel bus format: rgb565 or rgb666 (config.ini [display] color_format).

**Returns:** Symbol rgb565 or rgb666.

```scheme
(gui-color-format)  ; => rgb565
```

<a id="api-gui-mono-colors"></a>
#### `gui-mono-colors`

`(gui-mono-colors [fg bg])`

*since 1.0.0*

Two-color custom palette: sets entries 0 = bg and 1 = fg and the custom scheme; returns (fg bg).

**Returns:** List (fg bg) of RGB565 fixnums: the ones set, or the brightest and darkest colors of the current palette (white and 2179 at 16 bits).

Meant for 1-bit color (`gui-color-bits` 1).

```scheme
(gui-mono-colors)  ; => (65535 2179)
(gui-mono-colors (gui-rgb 255 176 0) 0)  ; => (64896 0)
(gui-color-scheme)  ; => custom
(gui-color-scheme 'color)
```

<a id="api-gui-palette-set_21"></a>
#### `gui-palette-set!`

`(gui-palette-set! index rgb565)`

*since 1.0.0*

Set palette entry 0..255 and switch to the custom scheme (starting from the current palette).

**Returns:** Void; ignored when an argument is not an integer or index is outside 0..255.

Only the first 2^bits entries are used (`gui-color-bits`). Queues a full redraw.

```scheme
(gui-color-bits 2)
(gui-palette-set! 3 (gui-rgb 255 0 0))
(list (gui-color-scheme) (gui-palette-get 3))  ; => (custom 63488)
(gui-color-scheme 'color)
(gui-color-bits 16)
```

<a id="api-gui-palette-get"></a>
#### `gui-palette-get`

`(gui-palette-get index)`

*since 1.0.0*

RGB565 color of a palette entry of the current scheme.

**Returns:** Fixnum; 0 for an index the palette does not have (at 16 bits the color scheme has no palette) or a non-integer index.

```scheme
(gui-palette-get 1)  ; => 0
(gui-color-bits 4)
(gui-palette-get 15)  ; => 65535
(gui-color-bits 16)
```

<a id="api-gui-palette-preset"></a>
#### `gui-palette-preset`

`(gui-palette-preset name)`

*since 1.0.0*

Legacy gui-color-scheme: set a scheme by name; #f for an unknown name.

**Returns:** #t when name (symbol or string) is a known scheme, else #f (no error).

```scheme
(gui-palette-preset 'gray)   ; => #t
(gui-palette-preset 'sepia)  ; => #f
(gui-palette-preset 'color)  ; => #t
```

<a id="api-gui-band-lines"></a>
#### `gui-band-lines`

`(gui-band-lines)`

*since 1.0.0*

Rows per band in band mode (config.ini [display] band_lines).

**Returns:** Fixnum: the band rows in band mode; in the other modes the configured value.

```scheme
(gui-band-lines)  ; => 20
```

<a id="api-gui-rgb"></a>
#### `gui-rgb`

`(gui-rgb r g b)`

*since 1.0.0*

RGB565 color of 8-bit red, green and blue (0..255).

**Returns:** Fixnum 0..65535: r and b keep 5 bits, g 6. Components wrap modulo 256; 0 unless all three are integers.

```scheme
(gui-rgb 255 0 0)      ; => 63488
(gui-rgb 255 255 255)  ; => 65535
(gui-rgb 11 17 24)     ; => 2179
```

<a id="api-gui-width"></a>
#### `gui-width`

`(gui-width)`

*since 1.0.0*

Screen width in pixels (320 in portrait, 480 in landscape).

**Returns:** Fixnum.

```scheme
(gui-width)  ; => 320
```

<a id="api-gui-height"></a>
#### `gui-height`

`(gui-height)`

*since 1.0.0*

Screen height in pixels (480 in portrait, 320 in landscape).

**Returns:** Fixnum.

```scheme
(gui-height)  ; => 480
```

<a id="api-gui-touch-poll"></a>
#### `gui-touch-poll`

`(gui-touch-poll)`

*since 1.0.0*

The touch point as (x . y) while the screen is touched, else #f.

**Returns:** Pair of fixnums or #f. Only the WASM simulator reports touches (a click on its canvas); the board has no touch panel: always #f.

```scheme
(gui-touch-poll)  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-gui-touch-down_3f"></a>
#### `gui-touch-down?`

`(gui-touch-down?)`

*since 1.0.0*

True while the screen is touched.

**Returns:** #t or #f (always #f on the board, see `gui-touch-poll`).

```scheme
(gui-touch-down?)  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-gui-invalidate"></a>
#### `gui-invalidate`

`(gui-invalidate [x y w h])`

*since 1.0.0*

Queue rows y..y+h-1 (the whole screen without arguments) to be redrawn by gui-render-proc.

**Returns:** Void. Only y and h count (whole rows are redrawn); (gui-invalidate y h) is also accepted.

The redraw happens after the current event, at the next display service: the runtime clears the queued rows to 2179 and calls `gui-render-proc` (no arguments) with drawing clipped to them. Queue only the rows that changed. Calls made while the render procedure runs are ignored.

```scheme
(define count 0)
(define (render) (gui-text-styled 10 10 (number->string count) 65535 0))
(define gui-render-proc render)
(set! count 1)
(gui-invalidate 0 0 320 30)
```

<a id="api-gui-visible_3f"></a>
#### `gui-visible?`

`(gui-visible? y h)`

*since 1.0.0*

Whether rows y..y+h-1 meet the area being drawn; skip the drawing of a section when #f.

**Returns:** #t or #f; #t when the arguments are not two integers.

Compares with the current clip: in `gui-render-proc` the rows being redrawn. In band mode the render procedure runs once for the whole span, so it skips sections outside what `gui-invalidate` queued.

```scheme
(gui-visible? 0 32)  ; => #t
(gui-set-clip 0 100 320 50)
(gui-visible? 0 32)  ; => #f
```

<a id="component-font"></a>
### Fonts (`font`)

Font slots: loading bitmap fonts and choosing them.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(font-load id path ['stream])`](#api-font-load) | stable |
| [`(font-register! id bytes)`](#api-font-register_21) | stable |
| [`(font-unload id)`](#api-font-unload) | stable |
| [`(font-info id)`](#api-font-info) | stable |
| [`(font-config [order [overrides]])`](#api-font-config) | stable |
| [`(font-sources id)`](#api-font-sources) | stable |
| [`(font-use id face [size])`](#api-font-use) | stable |

<a id="api-font-load"></a>
#### `font-load`

`(font-load id path ['stream])`

*since 1.0.0*

Load an MFNT font file (tools/make_font.py) into slot 2..7. Small files go to RAM; large ones (or 'stream) are read glyph by glyph. An app loads only files of its own folder.

**Returns:** #t. An error when id is not 2..7, path is not a string, or the file cannot be read or is not a valid MFNT font.

Needs an MFNT file on the board (or the simulator's file system). Files up to 24 KB are read into RAM on the board; larger ones stay on flash behind a glyph cache. The slot then holds only that font; loading queues a full redraw.

```scheme
(font-load 3 "/spiffs/fonts/simhei-24.mfnt")  ; => #t
(gui-text-styled 10 10 "Hello" 65535 3)
(font-load 1 "/spiffs/fonts/simhei-24.mfnt")  ; => error: font id must be 2..7
```

<a id="api-font-register_21"></a>
#### `font-register!`

`(font-register! id bytes)`

*since 1.0.0*

Use MFNT font bytes for slot 2..7, e.g. (include-bytes "x.mfnt"); a Code ROM literal is read in place, a heap string copied.

**Returns:** #t when the slot holds a font afterwards. An error when id is not 2..7, bytes is not a string or not a valid MFNT font.

The font's name (stored in it) also brings the other sources of config.ini [fonts] font_order (font ROM, files) to fill glyphs it lacks. Queues a full redraw.

```scheme
(font-register! 3 (include-bytes "fonts/digits-48.mfnt"))  ; => #t
(font-register! 3 "not a font")  ; => error: font-register!
```

<a id="api-font-unload"></a>
#### `font-unload`

`(font-unload id)`

*since 1.0.0*

Empty font slot 2..7; its text falls back to the system font.

**Returns:** Void. An error when id is not 2..7.

```scheme
(font-unload 3)
(font-info 3)    ; => #f
(font-unload 0)  ; => error: font id must be 2..7
```

<a id="api-font-info"></a>
#### `font-info`

`(font-info id)`

*since 1.0.0*

(name height glyphs source bytes) of a font slot; #f for an empty slot.

**Returns:** List: name string, height in pixels, glyph count, source symbol (builtin, rom, ram, file or fontrom: the first source of the chain) and the bytes it holds (0 for builtin). #f for an empty slot or a non-integer id.

Slots 0 and 1 report builtin unless config.ini [fonts] font_override replaces them.

```scheme
(font-info 0)  ; => ("system_16" 16 406 builtin 0)
(font-info 5)  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-font-config"></a>
#### `font-config`

`(font-config [order [overrides]])`

*since 1.0.0*

Font sources and replacements (config.ini [fonts] font_order, font_override); with arguments set them and resolve every font again.

**Returns:** List (sources overrides): the source symbols in order and a list of ("name" . "replacement") pairs. An error for an unknown source, a source listed twice, or an override not written name:replacement.

Sources: app (fonts the app carries), fontrom (the system font ROM), spiffs (/spiffs/fonts/<name>.mfnt). An override puts the sources of the replacement first; system_16 (or 0) and clock_32 (or 1) name the built-in fonts. Kept until the next boot; queues a full redraw.

```scheme
(font-config)  ; => ((app fontrom spiffs) ())
(font-config "fontrom, app" "system_16:simsun-16")  ; => ((fontrom app) (("system_16" . "simsun-16")))
(font-config "app, fontrom, spiffs" "")  ; => ((app fontrom spiffs) ())
(font-config "web")  ; => error: font_order
```

<a id="api-font-sources"></a>
#### `font-sources`

`(font-sources id)`

*since 1.0.0*

The chain searched for each glyph of slot id, in order, as ((source name height glyphs bits) ...).

**Returns:** List of lists: source symbol (rom, ram, file, fontrom), name, height, glyph count and bits per pixel (1, 2 or 4). () for an empty slot or a built-in font.

A glyph no source has comes from the system font.

```scheme
(font-sources 0)  ; => ()
```

<a id="api-font-use"></a>
#### `font-use`

`(font-use id face [size])`

*since 1.0.0 · older names: `use-font`*

Font slot 2..7 for this app: face-size from the app's embedded subset, the font ROM or a file (config.ini [fonts] font_order). #f when no source has it.

**Returns:** #t when slot id holds a font afterwards (also when it already held one: the slot is not changed), else #f and its text uses the system font. An error when id is not 2..7 or face is not a string.

tools/build_apps.py embeds a subset of the face (the characters of the app's strings) unless the form ends with 'system or the build uses --system-fonts. At run time the name <face>-<size> is looked up in the sources of font_order (app, fontrom, spiffs): the font the app carries, the system font ROM, /spiffs/fonts/<face>-<size>.mfnt. A face with a '/' is a file path. Queues a full redraw when it fills the slot.

```scheme
(define f (if (font-use 3 "simhei" 24) 3 0))
f  ; => 0
(font-use 1 "simhei" 24)  ; => error: font id must be 2..7
```

<a id="component-fontrom"></a>
### Font ROM (`fontrom`)

The system font ROM partition, read in place.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(fontrom-list)`](#api-fontrom-list) | stable |
| [`(fontrom-info)`](#api-fontrom-info) | stable |
| [`(fontrom-add path [name])`](#api-fontrom-add) | stable |
| [`(fontrom-remove name)`](#api-fontrom-remove) | stable |

<a id="api-fontrom-list"></a>
#### `fontrom-list`

`(fontrom-list)`

*since 1.0.0*

Fonts in the system font ROM (flash partition, read in place) as ((name height glyphs bytes) ...).

**Returns:** List of lists: name string, height in pixels, glyph count, size in bytes; () without a font ROM partition.

On a board with a font ROM it gives e.g. (("msyh-16" 16 7000 250000) ...). `font-use` finds the fonts by name <face>-<size>.

```scheme
(fontrom-list)  ; => ()
```

<a id="api-fontrom-info"></a>
#### `fontrom-info`

`(fontrom-info)`

*since 1.0.0*

(used capacity count) of the system font ROM: bytes used, partition bytes, fonts.

**Returns:** List of three fixnums; #f when the firmware has no fontrom partition (the WASM simulator and the PC build have none).

```scheme
(fontrom-info)  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-fontrom-add"></a>
#### `fontrom-add`

`(fontrom-add path [name])`

*since 1.0.0*

Copy an MFNT font file into the system font ROM (name defaults to the one in the font; the same name replaces it). Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).

**Returns:** String, the name stored. An error when path or name is not a string, there is no font ROM partition, or the file cannot be read, is not a font or does not fit.

On the board: `(fontrom-add "/spiffs/fonts/simhei-24.mfnt")` => "simhei-24". Slots using font ROM fonts are resolved again; queues a full redraw.

```scheme
(fontrom-add "/spiffs/fonts/simhei-24.mfnt")  ; => error: no font ROM partition
```

<a id="api-fontrom-remove"></a>
#### `fontrom-remove`

`(fontrom-remove name)`

*since 1.0.0*

Remove a font from the system font ROM; later fonts move down. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).

**Returns:** #t when removed, #f when there is no such font (or no font ROM). An error when name is not a string or the flash write fails.

```scheme
(fontrom-remove "simhei-24")  ; => #f
```

<a id="component-lunar"></a>
### Lunar calendar (`lunar`)

Chinese lunar dates computed on the device.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(lunar-date year month day)`](#api-lunar-date) | stable |
| [`(lunar-date-string year month day)`](#api-lunar-date-string) | stable |

<a id="api-lunar-date"></a>
#### `lunar-date`

`(lunar-date year month day)`

*since 1.0.0*

The Chinese lunar date of a Gregorian date as (month day leap?).

**Returns:** List: lunar month 1..12, day 1..30, #t in a leap month. #f for dates before 1900-01-31 or after 2100, months outside 1..12, days outside 1..31 or non-integer arguments.

The day is not checked against the month: 2024-02-30 counts as 2024-03-01.

```scheme
(lunar-date 2024 2 10)   ; => (1 1 #f)
(lunar-date 2023 3 22)   ; => (2 1 #t)
(lunar-date 1899 12 31)  ; => #f
```

<a id="api-lunar-date-string"></a>
#### `lunar-date-string`

`(lunar-date-string year month day)`

*since 1.0.0*

The lunar date as Chinese display text for the screen.

**Returns:** String "农历" + optional "闰" (leap) + month + "月" + day; #f where `lunar-date` gives #f.

```scheme
(lunar-date-string 2024 2 10)  ; => "农历正月初一"
(lunar-date-string 2023 3 22)  ; => "农历闰二月初一"
```

<a id="component-theme"></a>
### Color schemes (`theme`)

The system color scheme file the app framework reads (gui.scm).

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(theme-css)`](#api-theme-css) | stable |

<a id="api-theme-css"></a>
#### `theme-css`

`(theme-css)`

*since 1.8.0*

The system color scheme file /spiffs/theme.css as a string; any app may read it (gui.scm resolves color aliases with it).

**Returns:** A string of the file (binary-safe), or #f when there is none or it is over 16 KB. Never fails. Apps write only their own folder: the file is written by the device page or the system settings.

The format is CSS-like: blocks named after a scheme (day, night, or a name of your own; * for every scheme) holding alias: value; pairs, a value being #rgb, #rrggbb, rgb(r, g, b) or another alias; /* comments */. An app may keep its own theme.css in its folder (read with fs-read), which wins over this file. The cascade, the built-in schemes and the day/night switch are in docs/applib.md of minischeme-apps.

```scheme
(fs-write "/spiffs/theme.css" "night { titlebar_bg: #152030; }")
(theme-css) ; => "night { titlebar_bg: #152030; }"
```
