<a id="api-wifi-connect"></a>
#### `wifi-connect`

`(wifi-connect ssid password)`

*since 1.0.0*

Join a WiFi network as a station. The connection completes in the background and is retried automatically when it drops. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).

**Returns:** #t when the attempt has started (poll `(wifi-connected?)` for the link); #f when ssid is empty, an argument is not a string or the WiFi driver failed to start. Never an error. The board joins the network of config.ini at boot by itself.

```scheme
(wifi-connect "home-ap" "secret123")   ; => #t
(let wait ((n 0))
  (if (and (not (wifi-connected?)) (< n 100))
      (begin (delay-ms 100) (wait (+ n 1)))))
(wifi-connected?)
```

<a id="api-wifi-ap"></a>
#### `wifi-ap`

`(wifi-ap ssid password)`

*since 1.0.0*

Start a WiFi access point beside the station (address 192.168.4.1); a password under 8 characters makes it open. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).

**Returns:** #t when the access point is up; #f when ssid is empty, an argument is not a string or the driver refused. Never an error. The station keeps its connection.

```scheme
(wifi-ap "minischeme-setup" "")   ; => #t
```

<a id="api-wifi-connected_3f"></a>
#### `wifi-connected?`

`(wifi-connected?)`

*since 1.0.0 · older names: `wifi-status`*

Whether the station is connected and has an IP address.

**Returns:** #t or #f. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (ip-label) (if (wifi-connected?) (wifi-ip) "offline"))
(wifi-disconnect)
(ip-label)   ; => "offline"
```

<a id="api-wifi-disconnect"></a>
#### `wifi-disconnect`

`(wifi-disconnect [reconnect?])`

*since 1.0.0*

Disconnect the station and stop the automatic reconnect; with #t the link drops and reconnects at once. Not for apps: only the system settings and the REPL may (an app gets an error).

**Returns:** Void. Never an error. The reconnect? argument is honored by the firmware only; the simulator and the PC mocks just disconnect.

```scheme
(wifi-disconnect)
(wifi-connected?)   ; => #f
(wifi-ip)           ; => "0.0.0.0"
```

<a id="api-wifi-ip"></a>
#### `wifi-ip`

`(wifi-ip)`

*since 1.0.0*

The station IP address as a dotted string.

**Returns:** A string such as "192.168.1.42"; "0.0.0.0" while not connected. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (ip-line) (string-append "IP " (wifi-ip)))
(wifi-disconnect)
(ip-line)   ; => "IP 0.0.0.0"
```

<a id="api-wifi-rssi"></a>
#### `wifi-rssi`

`(wifi-rssi)`

*since 1.0.0*

Signal strength of the connected network in dBm.

**Returns:** A negative integer such as -52 (dBm; closer to 0 is stronger); 0 while not connected. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (wifi-bars)
  (let ((r (wifi-rssi)))
    (cond ((= r 0) 0) ((> r -55) 3) ((> r -70) 2) (else 1))))
(wifi-disconnect)
(wifi-bars)   ; => 0
```

<a id="api-wifi-ssid"></a>
#### `wifi-ssid`

`(wifi-ssid)`

*since 1.0.0*

The SSID of the connected network.

**Returns:** A string; "" while not connected. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (network-name) (let ((s (wifi-ssid))) (if (string=? s "") "-" s)))
(wifi-disconnect)
(network-name)   ; => "-"
```

<a id="component-json-feed"></a>
### JSON feed (`json-feed`)

Background HTTP polling of a JSON document, parsed into compact rows.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(json-feed-start url interval-ms keys selectors [pool-bytes [value-len [depth]]])`](#api-json-feed-start) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-ints i k)`](#api-json-feed-ints) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-stop)`](#api-json-feed-stop) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-seq)`](#api-json-feed-seq) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-count)`](#api-json-feed-count) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-selector i)`](#api-json-feed-selector) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-field i k)`](#api-json-feed-field) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-url)`](#api-json-feed-url) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-status)`](#api-json-feed-status) | stable |
| [`(json-feed-dump)`](#api-json-feed-dump) | stable |

<a id="api-json-feed-start"></a>
#### `json-feed-start`

`(json-feed-start url interval-ms keys selectors [pool-bytes [value-len [depth]]])`

*since 1.0.0*

Poll a JSON URL in the background; keep objects whose captured key matches a selector (key-index 'equal|'prefix string). A new call replaces the feed and fetches at once. An https:// URL goes through the protocol converter (config.ini [app] https_proxy, else proxy) as <it>/fetch?url=...; the board's own address is refused.

**Returns:** #t once the feed is configured. Errors: "json-feed-start: expected url interval-ms keys selectors ..." (url not a string, interval-ms not an integer), "keys must be strings", "selector must be (key-index 'equal|'prefix string)" (key-index not a key, another mode), "out of memory". interval-ms under 200 counts as 200. pool-bytes (value text per document), value-len (bytes per value) and depth (nesting levels captured) are limits the app chooses: omitted, 0 or #f means none (since 1.2.0; before, they were clamped to 256..16384, 16..256 and 1..8 with defaults 1536, 40 and 8). Any number of keys and selectors, of any length.

**Model.** One feed per device. On the board a background task fetches the URL
with an HTTP GET (redirects are not followed; timeout: interval-ms clamped to
3..15 s) and streams the response through a JSON scanner: the document itself
is never held in RAM. A failed fetch is retried within 5 s, a good one after
interval-ms (at least 200 ms). The WASM simulator fetches for the feed through
the page (web_repl/server.py serves the app proxy's `/app/` routes); the PC REPL
and the test VM have no fetcher, so their feed never gets a document. A new
`json-feed-start` replaces the whole configuration and the board fetches the
new URL at once (an app switching pages); documents of an older configuration
are never shown: `json-feed-seq` returns 0 until the first document of the new
one is taken.

**Capture.** `keys` names any number of keys of any length; key k is the
k-th name. Every JSON object nested at most `depth` objects deep (the
top-level object is depth 1; arrays do not count; no depth: every level) is
scanned for those keys; their scalar values are captured as text: strings
unescaped (UTF-8), numbers, `true`, `false` and `null` as written. With a
value-len, at most that many bytes of a value are kept (cut at a UTF-8
character boundary); without one, values are kept whole. Objects and arrays
are not values.

**Selection.** A selector is `(key-index mode string [keep-key ...])`, mode
`'equal` or `'prefix`; there may be any number of them. A captured object
becomes a row when the value of key key-index equals (or starts with) the
string; the first matching selector wins and `(json-feed-selector i)` tells
which. The optional keep-keys limit the values stored for that row (all
captured keys when omitted): `(0 equal "error" 1)` keeps only key 1.
`(0 prefix "")` keeps every object that has key 0. A document keeps any
number of rows; with a pool-bytes, at most that much value text. When rows or
text do not fit (pool-bytes, or memory: on the board the feed leaves 16 KB of
heap free for the system) the status reports `truncated` #t. A document in
which no object had a captured key counts as a failed fetch ("no matching JSON
objects in the response").

**Reading.** `(json-feed-seq)` takes the newest complete document; `count`,
`field`, `ints` and `selector` then read that document, unchanged until a later
`json-feed-seq` takes the next one. Call it once per tick and redraw when the
number changes. `field` and `ints` take a key's index or (since 1.2.0) its name.

**With the app proxy.** tools/app_proxy.py turns web APIs into flat documents
`{"items":[{"t":type,"a":..,"b":..,"c":..,"d":..,"e":..}]}` with series as
comma-separated integers; an app may name more keys (applib `app-keys!`).
apps/lib/applib.scm starts the feed with
`(json-feed-start url interval APP-KEYS '((0 prefix "")) 0 0 2)` and reads
every row with `json-feed-field` (`json-feed-ints` for series).

**Memory.** Nothing has a fixed size: the scanner's buffers (one per nesting
level), two snapshots (the one being filled and the one being read) and the
selectors are allocated as a feed needs them and kept for the next document.
`(json-feed-status)` reports the bytes held (`memory`). Until 1.2.0 a feed had
at most 6 keys of 23 bytes, 40 selectors, 64 rows, 16 KB of text, values of
255 bytes, 8 levels and a 255-byte URL.

```scheme
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance" 300000
                 '("t" "a" "b")
                 '((0 equal "news") (0 equal "error" 1))
                 2048 128 2)   ; => #t
(json-feed-url)   ; => "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance"
```

<a id="api-json-feed-ints"></a>
#### `json-feed-ints`

`(json-feed-ints i k)`

*since 1.0.0*

Integers of a comma-separated value of row i, key k: "12,-3,7" => (12 -3 7), or #f.

**Returns:** A list of integers (any number; a part without digits is skipped, "2.5" counts as 2); () for an empty value; #f when row i or its key k does not exist in the taken document. k is an index or (since 1.2.0) a key name. Never an error.

```scheme
;; a proxy row {"t":"temp","a":"Mon","b":"12,15,9,-3"} gives (12 15 9 -3)
(define (series i) (or (json-feed-ints i 2) '()))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/weather?loc=auto" 600000
                 '("t" "a" "b") '((0 prefix "")))
(series 0)   ; => ()
```

<a id="api-json-feed-stop"></a>
#### `json-feed-stop`

`(json-feed-stop)`

*since 1.0.0*

Stop polling: the fetcher idles. The document already taken stays readable.

**Returns:** Void. Never an error.

```scheme
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/ping" 60000 '("t") '((0 prefix "")))
(json-feed-stop)
(json-feed-url)                            ; => #f
(cdr (assq 'state (json-feed-status)))     ; => idle
```

<a id="api-json-feed-seq"></a>
#### `json-feed-seq`

`(json-feed-seq)`

*since 1.0.0*

Take the newest complete document, if one arrived; returns its number (0 = none yet).

**Returns:** An integer: the number of the document now readable (one higher per document taken); 0 while the current feed (since the last json-feed-start) has no document. Never an error.

```scheme
(define last-seq 0)
(define (feed-poll! redraw)
  (let ((seq (json-feed-seq)))
    (if (and (> seq 0) (not (= seq last-seq)))
        (begin (set! last-seq seq) (redraw)))))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/ping" 60000 '("t") '((0 prefix "")))
(json-feed-seq)   ; => 0
```

<a id="api-json-feed-count"></a>
#### `json-feed-count`

`(json-feed-count)`

*since 1.0.0*

Rows (selected objects) of the taken document.

**Returns:** An integer, 0 or more; 0 before the current feed has a document. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (feed-titles)
  (let loop ((i (- (json-feed-count) 1)) (acc '()))
    (if (< i 0) acc (loop (- i 1) (cons (json-feed-field i 1) acc)))))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance" 300000
                 '("t" "a") '((0 equal "news")))
(feed-titles)   ; => ()
```

<a id="api-json-feed-selector"></a>
#### `json-feed-selector`

`(json-feed-selector i)`

*since 1.0.0*

Index of the selector that row i matched.

**Returns:** An integer (0 for the first selector of json-feed-start); #f when row i does not exist in the taken document. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (row-kind i)
  (case (json-feed-selector i) ((0) 'news) ((1) 'error) (else #f)))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance" 300000
                 '("t" "a") '((0 equal "news") (0 equal "error")))
(row-kind 0)   ; => #f
```

<a id="api-json-feed-field"></a>
#### `json-feed-field`

`(json-feed-field i k)`

*since 1.0.0*

Captured value of key k (an index into keys, or since 1.2.0 a key name) for row i, as a string, or #f.

**Returns:** A string: the value as text (strings unescaped, numbers and true/false/null as written), whole or at most value-len bytes; #f when row i does not exist, the object lacked key k (or k names no key), or the selector did not keep it. Never an error.

```scheme
;; row {"t":"news","a":"Markets rally","b":"10:42"}: (json-feed-field i 1) => "Markets rally"
(define (field-or i k default) (or (json-feed-field i k) default))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance" 300000
                 '("t" "a" "b") '((0 equal "news")))
(field-or 0 1 "(loading)")   ; => "(loading)"
;; by name, the same key as index 1:
(json-feed-field 0 "a")      ; => #f
```

<a id="api-json-feed-url"></a>
#### `json-feed-url`

`(json-feed-url)`

*since 1.0.0*

The URL being polled, or #f.

**Returns:** A string: the URL of the last json-feed-start; #f before any or after json-feed-stop. Never an error.

```scheme
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/ping" 60000 '("t") '((0 prefix "")))
(json-feed-url)   ; => "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/ping"
```

<a id="api-json-feed-status"></a>
#### `json-feed-status`

`(json-feed-status)`

*since 1.0.0*

Feed state as an alist: state, error, fetches, failures, bytes, fetch-ms, age-ms, objects, truncated, memory.

**Returns:** An alist in this order: (state . idle|connecting|ok|error), (error . message of the last failed fetch, "" after a good one: "WiFi not connected", "cannot connect", "HTTP status 404", "read error after N bytes", "no matching JSON objects in the response"), (fetches . n) and (failures . n) since boot, (bytes . size of the last response), (fetch-ms . duration of the last fetch, board only, else 0), (age-ms . ms since the last good document, -1 if none), (objects . objects with a captured key in the taken document), (truncated . #t when rows or value text did not fit: pool-bytes, value-len or memory), (memory . bytes the feed holds, since 1.2.0). Never an error.

```scheme
(define (feed-stat key) (cdr (assq key (json-feed-status))))
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/ping" 60000 '("t") '((0 prefix "")))
(feed-stat 'state)    ; => connecting
(feed-stat 'age-ms)   ; => -1
```

<a id="api-json-feed-dump"></a>
#### `json-feed-dump`

`(json-feed-dump)`

*since 1.0.0*

Every object of a document with captured keys, values joined by TAB, one per line.

**Returns:** A string (as long as the document needs, memory permitting): one line per object that had any captured key, selected or not, its values in key order joined by TAB. On the board it waits up to 6 s for the next fetched document; the simulator lists the last one. #f when no document came (or no feed was started). Never an error.

```scheme
(json-feed-start "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/news?cat=finance" 300000
                 '("t" "a") '((0 equal "news")))
(display (or (json-feed-dump) "no document\n"))
;; prints one line per object, e.g. news<TAB>Markets rally
```

<a id="component-http"></a>
### HTTP (`http`)

Direct HTTP requests.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(http-get url [headers])`](#api-http-get) | reserved |
| [`(http-post url body [content-type])`](#api-http-post) | reserved |

<a id="api-http-get"></a>
#### `http-get`

`(http-get url [headers])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'http-get)` is `#f`)*

Fetch a URL and wait for the response: (status . body).

**Returns:** A pair (status . body): status the HTTP status as an integer (any status, 404 too, is a result; redirects are not followed), body the response body as a string of its bytes. headers: an alist of (name . value) strings. Blocks the app until the response is complete, at most 10 s. Errors: "http-get: WiFi not connected", "http-get: cannot connect", "http-get: timeout", "http-get: response larger than 16384 bytes", a url not http:// or https://.

```scheme
(let ((r (http-get "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/ping"
                   '(("Accept" . "application/json")))))
  (if (= (car r) 200) (json-parse (cdr r)) #f))
; => ((items . #(((t . "ok")))))
```

<a id="api-http-post"></a>
#### `http-post`

`(http-post url body [content-type])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'http-post)` is `#f`)*

Post a string body and wait for the response: (status . body).

**Returns:** A pair (status . body) as http-get. content-type defaults to "application/json". Blocks the app until the response is complete, at most 10 s. Errors as http-get, prefixed "http-post:".

```scheme
(define r (http-post "http://192.168.1.10:8087/log"
                     (json-stringify '((device . "kitchen") (temp . 21)))))
(car r)
; => 200
```

<a id="component-mqtt"></a>
### MQTT (`mqtt`)

MQTT client.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(mqtt-connect url [client-id])`](#api-mqtt-connect) | reserved |
| [`(mqtt-disconnect)`](#api-mqtt-disconnect) | reserved |
| [`(mqtt-publish topic payload [qos [retain?]])`](#api-mqtt-publish) | reserved |
| [`(mqtt-subscribe topic [qos])`](#api-mqtt-subscribe) | reserved |
| [`(mqtt-poll)`](#api-mqtt-poll) | reserved |

<a id="api-mqtt-connect"></a>
#### `mqtt-connect`

`(mqtt-connect url [client-id])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'mqtt-connect)` is `#f`)*

Connect to a broker (mqtt:// or mqtts://, user:password@ allowed); reconnects by itself later.

**Returns:** #t once the broker accepted the connection (waits at most 10 s). client-id defaults to "minischeme-" and the last 6 hex digits of the MAC. A second call replaces the connection. After a drop the client reconnects and subscribes again by itself. Errors: "mqtt-connect: WiFi not connected", "cannot connect", "timeout", "refused by the broker (code N)".

```scheme
(mqtt-connect "mqtt://user:pass@192.168.1.10:1883" "kitchen-display")
; => #t
```

<a id="api-mqtt-disconnect"></a>
#### `mqtt-disconnect`

`(mqtt-disconnect)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'mqtt-disconnect)` is `#f`)*

Close the connection; forget subscriptions and queued messages.

**Returns:** Void; also when not connected. Never an error.

```scheme
(mqtt-disconnect)
```

<a id="api-mqtt-publish"></a>
#### `mqtt-publish`

`(mqtt-publish topic payload [qos [retain?]])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'mqtt-publish)` is `#f`)*

Publish a string payload to a topic.

**Returns:** #t once the message is handed to the client (QoS 1 and 2 are delivered with retries in the background). qos 0, 1 or 2 (default 0); retain? default #f. Errors: "mqtt-publish: not connected", "qos must be 0, 1 or 2", a topic or payload not a string.

```scheme
(mqtt-publish "home/kitchen/temp" (number->string 21) 1 #t)
; => #t
```

<a id="api-mqtt-subscribe"></a>
#### `mqtt-subscribe`

`(mqtt-subscribe topic [qos])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'mqtt-subscribe)` is `#f`)*

Subscribe to a topic filter (+ and # wildcards); messages queue for mqtt-poll.

**Returns:** #t once the broker acknowledged the subscription. qos 0, 1 or 2 (default 0). Subscriptions are renewed after a reconnect. Errors: "mqtt-subscribe: not connected", "qos must be 0, 1 or 2", "refused by the broker".

```scheme
(mqtt-subscribe "home/+/temp")
; => #t
```

<a id="api-mqtt-poll"></a>
#### `mqtt-poll`

`(mqtt-poll)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'mqtt-poll)` is `#f`)*

The next message received: (topic . payload), or #f.

**Returns:** A pair of strings (topic . payload), oldest first; #f when the queue is empty or not connected. The queue keeps 16 messages; when full the oldest is dropped. Never an error.

```scheme
(let loop ((m (mqtt-poll)))
  (if m
      (begin (show-reading (car m) (string->number (cdr m)))
             (loop (mqtt-poll)))))
```

## Storage

<a id="component-fs"></a>
### File system (`fs`)

Files under /spiffs (LittleFS on the board).

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(fs-read path)`](#api-fs-read) | stable |
| [`(fs-write path str)`](#api-fs-write) | stable |
| [`(fs-exists? path)`](#api-fs-exists_3f) | stable |
| [`(fs-remove path)`](#api-fs-remove) | stable |
| [`(fs-info)`](#api-fs-info) | stable |
| [`(fs-list dir)`](#api-fs-list) | stable |
| [`(fs-download url path)`](#api-fs-download) | stable |
| [`(fs-download-status)`](#api-fs-download-status) | stable |
| [`(fs-rename from to)`](#api-fs-rename) | reserved |
| [`(fs-append path data)`](#api-fs-append) | reserved |
| [`(fs-size path)`](#api-fs-size) | reserved |

<a id="api-fs-read"></a>
#### `fs-read`

`(fs-read path)`

*since 1.0.0*

Read a whole file as a string.

**Returns:** A string of the file's bytes (binary-safe: NUL bytes included); #f when the file cannot be opened (missing) or path is not a string. Never an error.

Files of the board's file system live under `/spiffs/` (LittleFS). An app may
touch only its own folder (`/spiffs/apps/<id>/`, or `/spiffs/user/<id>/` for an
uploaded app): a relative path such as `"notes.txt"` is in that folder, an
absolute one must be; its image there (app.msbc) is read-only and the folder
holds at most config.ini [system] app_storage_kb (256 KB, the image included).
Anything else is an error. The system settings and code from the REPL are not
limited (relative paths are then under `/spiffs`). The WASM simulator keeps its
files in the page and accepts only paths under `/spiffs/` (at most 63 bytes, no
`..`); the PC REPL and the test VM keep them in memory. Strings are byte
strings, so any UTF-8 text round-trips.

```scheme
(fs-write "/spiffs/note.txt" "buy milk")
(fs-read "/spiffs/note.txt")      ; => "buy milk"
(fs-read "/spiffs/missing.txt")   ; => #f
```

<a id="api-fs-write"></a>
#### `fs-write`

`(fs-write path str)`

*since 1.0.0*

Create or replace a file with the bytes of a string.

**Returns:** #t when the whole string was written; #f when the file cannot be created (missing directory, file system full, in the simulator a path outside /spiffs/) or an argument is not a string. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (save-count! n) (fs-write "/spiffs/count.txt" (number->string n)))
(save-count! 42)                                 ; => #t
(string->number (fs-read "/spiffs/count.txt"))   ; => 42
```

<a id="api-fs-exists_3f"></a>
#### `fs-exists?`

`(fs-exists? path)`

*since 1.0.0*

Whether a file exists (paths under /spiffs/).

**Returns:** #t when the file exists and can be opened; #f otherwise or when path is not a string. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (load-or path default) (if (fs-exists? path) (fs-read path) default))
(load-or "/spiffs/city.txt" "Shanghai")   ; => "Shanghai"
(fs-write "/spiffs/city.txt" "Beijing")
(load-or "/spiffs/city.txt" "Shanghai")   ; => "Beijing"
```

<a id="api-fs-remove"></a>
#### `fs-remove`

`(fs-remove path)`

*since 1.0.0*

Delete a file.

**Returns:** #t when the file was deleted; #f when it does not exist, cannot be deleted or path is not a string. Never an error.

```scheme
(fs-write "/spiffs/tmp.txt" "x")
(fs-remove "/spiffs/tmp.txt")    ; => #t
(fs-remove "/spiffs/tmp.txt")    ; => #f
(fs-exists? "/spiffs/tmp.txt")   ; => #f
```

<a id="api-fs-info"></a>
#### `fs-info`

`(fs-info)`

*since 1.0.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

Total and used bytes of the file system: (total used).

**Returns:** A list of two integers (total used) in bytes. Never an error.

```scheme
(let* ((info (fs-info)) (free (- (car info) (cadr info))))
  (string-append (number->string (quotient free 1024)) " KB free"))
; e.g. "1210 KB free"
```

<a id="api-fs-list"></a>
#### `fs-list`

`(fs-list dir)`

*since 1.0.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

Files directly in a directory with their sizes: (("name" . bytes) ...).

**Returns:** A list of pairs (name . size) for the regular files directly in dir (subdirectories are left out; names without the directory); () when dir does not exist or is not /spiffs or under /spiffs/. Error "fs-list: expected a directory path" when dir is missing or not a string.

```scheme
(map car (fs-list "/spiffs/apps"))
; e.g. ("weather.msbc" "stocks.msbc")
(apply + (map cdr (fs-list "/spiffs")))
```

<a id="api-fs-download"></a>
#### `fs-download`

`(fs-download url path)`

*since 1.10.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

Download a file from the network into the app's folder, in the background (an image for gui-image, for example); one download at a time.

**Returns:** #t when the download is queued; #f while another download is still running (try again after it, see fs-download-status). Errors: url not http:// or https://, path outside the app's folder (the same rule as fs-write), the app's storage full.

The board fetches over plain HTTP like the JSON feed (the device headers go to configured servers; an https:// URL goes through the protocol converter), after the feed's current request. The body is written to path.part and replaces path only when complete: a failed download leaves the old file. At most 256 KB, and no more than the app's storage quota has left. gui-image draws baseline JPEG only: let the app server convert pictures (size and format) before the board downloads them. In the WebREPL simulator the page fetches the file through server.py.

```scheme
;; a picture from the app server into the app's folder, then drawn
(fs-download (string-append (app-url "/app/myapp/pic?id=7")) "cache/7.jpg")   ; => #t
;; later, in app-step or app-tick-proc:
(if (eq? (cdr (assq 'state (fs-download-status))) 'done)
    (gui-invalidate 0 0 320 480))   ; render then draws (gui-image x y "cache/7.jpg")
```

<a id="api-fs-download-status"></a>
#### `fs-download-status`

`(fs-download-status)`

*since 1.10.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

The state of the last fs-download: (state path bytes error seq) as an alist.

**Returns:** An alist: (state . s) with s one of idle, queued, running, done, error; (path . "the path given"); (bytes . n) written when done; (error . "message") when it failed ("" otherwise); (seq . k), which grows by one each time a download ends (done or error), so a change means a new outcome. Never an error.

```scheme
(define (download-state) (cdr (assq 'state (fs-download-status))))
(download-state)   ; => idle
```

<a id="api-fs-rename"></a>
#### `fs-rename`

`(fs-rename from to)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'fs-rename)` is `#f`)*

Rename or move a file; an existing target is not replaced.

**Returns:** #t when renamed; #f when from does not exist, to already exists or the file system refuses. Error "fs-rename: expected two path strings" when an argument is not a string.

```scheme
(fs-write "/spiffs/log.tmp" "boot ok\n")
(fs-rename "/spiffs/log.tmp" "/spiffs/log.txt")   ; => #t
(fs-exists? "/spiffs/log.tmp")                    ; => #f
```

<a id="api-fs-append"></a>
#### `fs-append`

`(fs-append path data)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'fs-append)` is `#f`)*

Append the bytes of a string to a file, creating it when missing.

**Returns:** #t when all of data was appended; #f when the file cannot be opened or written (file system full). Error "fs-append: expected a path and a string" when an argument is not a string.

```scheme
(define (log! line) (fs-append "/spiffs/events.log" (string-append line "\n")))
(log! "button pressed")   ; => #t
```

<a id="api-fs-size"></a>
#### `fs-size`

`(fs-size path)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'fs-size)` is `#f`)*

Size of a file in bytes, or #f.

**Returns:** An integer (bytes); #f when the file does not exist. Error "fs-size: expected a path string" when path is not a string.

```scheme
(fs-write "/spiffs/note.txt" "hello")
(fs-size "/spiffs/note.txt")      ; => 5
(fs-size "/spiffs/missing.txt")   ; => #f
```

<a id="component-kv"></a>
### Key-value store (`kv`)

Small persistent values (NVS on the board).

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(kv-get key [default])`](#api-kv-get) | reserved |
| [`(kv-set! key value)`](#api-kv-set_21) | reserved |
| [`(kv-remove key)`](#api-kv-remove) | reserved |
| [`(kv-keys)`](#api-kv-keys) | reserved |

<a id="api-kv-get"></a>
#### `kv-get`

`(kv-get key [default])`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'kv-get)` is `#f`)*

A value stored with kv-set! (a string), or default. Each app has its own keys.

**Returns:** The stored string; default (#f when omitted) when the key is not stored. key: a string or symbol of 1..15 bytes, else error "kv-get: key must be 1..15 bytes". Keys belong to the running app (its id is the namespace).

```scheme
(define city (kv-get "city" "Shanghai"))
(kv-set! "city" "Beijing")
(kv-get "city")   ; => "Beijing"
```

<a id="api-kv-set_21"></a>
#### `kv-set!`

`(kv-set! key value)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'kv-set!)` is `#f`)*

Store a string under a key, kept across restarts (NVS on the board).

**Returns:** #t once the value is committed to flash. Errors: "kv-set!: key must be 1..15 bytes", "value must be a string of at most 4000 bytes", "store full".

```scheme
(kv-set! "volume" (number->string 7))          ; => #t
(string->number (kv-get "volume" "5"))         ; => 7
```

<a id="api-kv-remove"></a>
#### `kv-remove`

`(kv-remove key)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'kv-remove)` is `#f`)*

Delete a key of the running app.

**Returns:** #t when the key was removed; #f when it was not stored. Error "kv-remove: key must be 1..15 bytes".

```scheme
(kv-set! "token" "abc")
(kv-remove "token")   ; => #t
(kv-get "token")      ; => #f
```

<a id="api-kv-keys"></a>
#### `kv-keys`

`(kv-keys)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'kv-keys)` is `#f`)*

The keys stored by the running app.

**Returns:** A list of key strings in no particular order; () when none. Never an error.

```scheme
(for-each kv-remove (kv-keys))
(kv-keys)   ; => ()
```

<a id="component-cfasl"></a>
### Compressed bytecode (`cfasl`)

CFASL compression of code and lazily loaded stubs.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(cfasl-compress byte-str)`](#api-cfasl-compress) | stable |
| [`(cfasl-decompress comp-str uncomp-size)`](#api-cfasl-decompress) | stable |
| [`(cfasl-make-stub comp-code code-bytes nparams max-stack variadic? inner-lambdas? constants)`](#api-cfasl-make-stub) | stable |
| [`(cfasl-call stub arg ...)`](#api-cfasl-call) | stable |
| [`(cfasl-stub? obj)`](#api-cfasl-stub_3f) | stable |

<a id="api-cfasl-compress"></a>
#### `cfasl-compress`

`(cfasl-compress byte-str)`

*since 1.0.0*

Compress a byte string with LZSS (4 KB window, matches of 3..18 bytes).

**Returns:** The compressed bytes as a string (keep the original length: cfasl-decompress needs it); () when byte-str is empty or not a string. Incompressible data can grow to twice its size (bytes >= 128 cost two bytes each). Never an error.

```scheme
(define s "ABCDEF1234567890ABCDEF1234567890")
(string-length (cfasl-compress s))   ; => 19
(cfasl-compress "")                  ; => ()
```

<a id="api-cfasl-decompress"></a>
#### `cfasl-decompress`

`(cfasl-decompress comp-str uncomp-size)`

*since 1.0.0*

Decompress LZSS bytes made by cfasl-compress; uncomp-size is the original length.

**Returns:** A string of exactly uncomp-size bytes (a smaller uncomp-size gives the first bytes); () when the data is corrupt or yields fewer bytes, or an argument has the wrong type. Never an error.

```scheme
(define s "ABCDEF1234567890ABCDEF1234567890")
(define c (cfasl-compress s))
(equal? (cfasl-decompress c (string-length s)) s)   ; => #t
(cfasl-decompress c 6)     ; => "ABCDEF"
(cfasl-decompress c 100)   ; => ()
```

<a id="api-cfasl-make-stub"></a>
#### `cfasl-make-stub`

`(cfasl-make-stub comp-code code-bytes nparams max-stack variadic? inner-lambdas? constants)`

*since 1.0.0*

Make a demand-paged procedure stub from compressed bytecode; cfasl-call decompresses and runs it.

**Returns:** The stub, a vector #(cfasl-stub comp-code code-bytes nparams max-stack variadic? inner-lambdas? constants); () when fewer than 7 arguments are given, comp-code is not a non-empty string or code-bytes (the uncompressed length) is not an integer. The bytecode is not checked: it must come from this VM version's compiler. Never an error.

```scheme
;; the bytecode of (lambda (x) x): GET_LOCAL 0, RETURN
(define code (cfasl-compress (list->string (map integer->char '(7 0 20)))))
(define id (cfasl-make-stub code 3 1 8 #f #f #()))
(cfasl-stub? id)     ; => #t
(cfasl-call id 42)   ; => 42
```

<a id="api-cfasl-call"></a>
#### `cfasl-call`

`(cfasl-call stub arg ...)`

*since 1.0.0*

Decompress the bytecode of a procedure stub and run it with the arguments.

**Returns:** The value the procedure returns (void when called without a stub). Errors: a wrong argument count ("cfasl-call: expected N arguments, got M"; at least N - 1 for a variadic procedure), a corrupt stub ("cfasl_call_chunk: invalid chunk stub", "expected cfasl-stub object", "corrupt compressed data", "cfasl-call: corrupt stub", "empty procedure"), "procedure chunk exceeds scratch buffer limit (N > 32768)", "decompression failure", "out of memory". The bytecode itself is trusted (made by the compiler).

```scheme
;; the bytecode of (lambda () 42): INT8 42, RETURN
(define code (cfasl-compress (list->string (map integer->char '(2 42 20)))))
(define answer (cfasl-make-stub code 3 0 8 #f #f #()))
(cfasl-call answer)            ; => 42
(cfasl-call (vector 1 2))      ; => error: invalid chunk stub
```

<a id="api-cfasl-stub_3f"></a>
#### `cfasl-stub?`

`(cfasl-stub? obj)`

*since 1.0.0*

Whether obj is a procedure stub made by cfasl-make-stub.

**Returns:** #t for a stub (a vector of 8 or more elements whose first is the symbol cfasl-stub), else #f. Never an error.

```scheme
(cfasl-stub? (cfasl-make-stub (cfasl-compress "abc") 3 0 8 #f #f #()))   ; => #t
(cfasl-stub? (vector 1 2 3))   ; => #f
```

## Tools

<a id="component-json"></a>
### JSON (`json`)

JSON text to Scheme data and back.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(json-parse text)`](#api-json-parse) | reserved |
| [`(json-stringify value)`](#api-json-stringify) | reserved |

<a id="api-json-parse"></a>
#### `json-parse`

`(json-parse text)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'json-parse)` is `#f`)*

JSON text to data: objects become alists with symbol keys, arrays vectors, null ().

**Returns:** The value of the JSON document (see the mapping). Errors: "json-parse: invalid JSON at byte N" (also for text after the value), "json-parse: nesting deeper than 32", text not a string.

Mapping (json-parse, and json-stringify back):

| JSON | Scheme |
|---|---|
| object `{"a":1}` | association list with symbol keys `((a . 1))`, members in document order |
| array `[1,2]` | vector `#(1 2)` |
| string | string (UTF-8; escapes decoded, `\uXXXX` surrogate pairs combined) |
| integer `42`, `-7` | exact integer (bignum when large) |
| number with `.` or exponent | flonum |
| `true` / `false` | `#t` / `#f` |
| `null` | `()` |

An empty object `{}` also parses to `()`, so it is written back as `null`.
json-stringify also accepts string keys and writes symbols in value position as
strings. Read members with `assq`: `(cdr (assq 'temp obj))`.

```scheme
(define doc (json-parse "{\"t\":\"temp\",\"v\":21.5,\"s\":[1,2],\"ok\":true,\"x\":null}"))
doc                      ; => ((t . "temp") (v . 21.5) (s . #(1 2)) (ok . #t) (x))
(cdr (assq 'v doc))      ; => 21.5
(json-parse "[1,")       ; => error: json-parse: invalid JSON at byte 3
```

<a id="api-json-stringify"></a>
#### `json-stringify`

`(json-stringify value)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'json-stringify)` is `#f`)*

Data to compact JSON text (the inverse of json-parse).

**Returns:** A string without whitespace: alists (symbol or string keys) become objects, vectors arrays, strings and symbols JSON strings (", \ and control characters escaped, UTF-8 kept), exact integers and finite flonums numbers, #t/#f true/false, () null. Error "json-stringify: cannot encode X" for anything else (procedures, characters, improper lists, NaN or infinities).

```scheme
(json-stringify '((t . "temp") (v . 21) (ok . #t) (s . #(1 2))))
; => "{\"t\":\"temp\",\"v\":21,\"ok\":true,\"s\":[1,2]}"
(json-stringify #(1 "a" ()))
; => "[1,\"a\",null]"
```

<a id="component-codec"></a>
### Encodings (`codec`)

Base64, URL encoding and checksums.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(base64-encode str)`](#api-base64-encode) | reserved |
| [`(base64-decode str)`](#api-base64-decode) | reserved |
| [`(url-encode str)`](#api-url-encode) | reserved |
| [`(url-decode str)`](#api-url-decode) | reserved |
| [`(crc32 str)`](#api-crc32) | reserved |

<a id="api-base64-encode"></a>
#### `base64-encode`

`(base64-encode str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'base64-encode)` is `#f`)*

Base64 text of a string's bytes (standard alphabet, = padding, no line breaks).

**Returns:** A string of Base64 text (RFC 4648 alphabet with + and /, padded with =); "" for "". Error "base64-encode: expected a string".

```scheme
(base64-encode "hello")                ; => "aGVsbG8="
(string-append "Basic " (base64-encode "user:pass"))
; => "Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz"
```

<a id="api-base64-decode"></a>
#### `base64-decode`

`(base64-decode str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'base64-decode)` is `#f`)*

The bytes of Base64 text as a string; padding optional, whitespace ignored.

**Returns:** A string of the decoded bytes. The = padding may be left out; spaces and line breaks are skipped. Error "base64-decode: invalid Base64" for another character or a wrong length, and for a str that is not a string.

```scheme
(base64-decode "aGVsbG8=")   ; => "hello"
(base64-decode "aGVsbG8")    ; => "hello"
```

<a id="api-url-encode"></a>
#### `url-encode`

`(url-encode str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'url-encode)` is `#f`)*

Percent-encode a string for a URL query: every byte but A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~ becomes %XX.

**Returns:** A string: unreserved characters (RFC 3986: letters, digits, - _ . ~) kept, every other byte as %XX with uppercase hex (a space is %20, UTF-8 characters byte by byte). Error "url-encode: expected a string".

```scheme
(url-encode "a b&c=d/é")   ; => "a%20b%26c%3Dd%2F%C3%A9"
(string-append "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/weather?loc=" (url-encode "New York"))
; => "http://192.168.1.10:8087/app/weather?loc=New%20York"
```

<a id="api-url-decode"></a>
#### `url-decode`

`(url-decode str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'url-decode)` is `#f`)*

Decode percent-encoding (and + as space).

**Returns:** A string: each %XX (either case) becomes its byte and + a space; a % not followed by two hex digits is kept as is. Error "url-decode: expected a string".

```scheme
(url-decode "a+b%26c%3d%E2%9C%93")   ; => "a b&c=✓"
(url-decode "100%")                  ; => "100%"
```

<a id="api-crc32"></a>
#### `crc32`

`(crc32 str)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'crc32)` is `#f`)*

CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, as zlib and PNG) of a string's bytes.

**Returns:** An exact integer 0..4294967295 (reflected polynomial #xEDB88320, initial value and final XOR #xFFFFFFFF). Error "crc32: expected a string".

```scheme
(crc32 "123456789")                 ; => 3421780262
(number->string (crc32 "") 16)      ; => "0"
```

<a id="component-random"></a>
### Random numbers (`random`)

Pseudo-random numbers.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(random n)`](#api-random) | reserved |
| [`(random-seed! n)`](#api-random-seed_21) | reserved |

<a id="api-random"></a>
#### `random`

`(random n)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'random)` is `#f`)*

A pseudo-random integer in 0..n-1.

**Returns:** An exact integer 0 <= r < n. Seeded from the hardware random generator at boot (other sequences every start) unless random-seed! is called. Error "random: expected a positive integer" when n is not an integer >= 1.

```scheme
(define colors #("red" "green" "blue"))
(vector-ref colors (random (vector-length colors)))
(< -1 (random 6) 6)   ; => #t
```

<a id="api-random-seed_21"></a>
#### `random-seed!`

`(random-seed! n)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'random-seed!)` is `#f`)*

Seed the generator: the same seed gives the same numbers on every device and the simulator.

**Returns:** Void. n: any exact integer (only its low 32 bits count). Error "random-seed!: expected an integer".

```scheme
(random-seed! 42)
(define a (list (random 100) (random 100)))
(random-seed! 42)
(equal? a (list (random 100) (random 100)))   ; => #t
```

<a id="api-esp32-mac"></a>
#### `esp32-mac`

`(esp32-mac)`

*since 1.0.0 · extension `esp32` 1.0.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

The factory MAC address of the WiFi station as "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff".

**Returns:** A string of 17 characters: six lowercase hex byte pairs joined by colons, read from the eFuse (the same on every boot, a unique device id). Never an error.

```scheme
(esp32-mac)                     ; e.g. "24:6f:28:a1:b2:c3"
(substring (esp32-mac) 9 17)    ; e.g. "a1:b2:c3"
(define device-id (if (api-has? 'esp32-mac) (esp32-mac) "unknown"))
```

<a id="api-esp32-reset-reason"></a>
#### `esp32-reset-reason`

`(esp32-reset-reason)`

*since 1.0.0 · extension `esp32` 1.0.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

Why the chip last started: 'power-on, 'software, 'panic, 'watchdog, 'brownout, 'deep-sleep or 'other.

**Returns:** A symbol: power-on (power or the reset pin), software ((restart) or a firmware update), panic (a crash), watchdog (a task or interrupt watchdog), brownout (supply voltage dropped), deep-sleep (woke from (deep-sleep)), other. Never an error.

```scheme
(if (memq (esp32-reset-reason) '(panic watchdog brownout))
    (display "restarted after a fault\n"))
```

<a id="api-esp32-idf-version"></a>
#### `esp32-idf-version`

`(esp32-idf-version)`

*since 1.0.0 · extension `esp32` 1.0.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

The ESP-IDF version the firmware was built with, e.g. "v6.1".

**Returns:** A string as the ESP-IDF reports it, e.g. "v6.1" (a development build may add a suffix such as "-dev-123-gabcdef"). Never an error.

```scheme
(esp32-idf-version)   ; e.g. "v6.1"
```

<a id="api-esp32-touch-read"></a>
#### `esp32-touch-read`

`(esp32-touch-read pad)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'esp32-touch-read)` is `#f`) · extension `esp32` 1.0.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

Raw value of a capacitive touch pad (0..9); lower when touched.

**Returns:** A non-negative integer, the raw charge count of pad T0..T9 (GPIO 4, 0, 2, 15, 13, 12, 14, 27, 33, 32); it drops when a finger is near, so compare it with an untouched reading. The first read of a pad sets it up. Error "esp32-touch-read: pad must be 0..9".

```scheme
(define idle (esp32-touch-read 0))
(define (touched?) (< (esp32-touch-read 0) (quotient (* idle 2) 3)))
```

<a id="api-esp32-psram-size"></a>
#### `esp32-psram-size`

`(esp32-psram-size)`

*since 1.0.0 · **reserved** (not implemented in 1.10.0; `(api-has? 'esp32-psram-size)` is `#f`) · extension `esp32` 1.0.0 · device only (firmware and WASM simulator)*

Bytes of external PSRAM, 0 without.

**Returns:** A non-negative integer: the size of the external PSRAM in bytes (e.g. 4194304), 0 on a board without one. Never an error.

```scheme
(define big-cache? (> (esp32-psram-size) 0))
```

<a id="component-host"></a>
### PC REPL (`host`)

Host files and processes; only in the PC REPL, never on a device.

| Procedure | Status |
|---|---|
| [`(fasl-to-c in out name exe?)`](#api-fasl-to-c) | stable |

<a id="api-fasl-to-c"></a>
#### `fasl-to-c`

`(fasl-to-c in out name exe?)`

*since 1.0.0 · PC REPL only*

Write a FASL file as an 8-byte aligned C array named name; with exe? #t also a main() that runs it.

**Returns:** #t when out was written; #f when in is empty or cannot be read in full. Errors: "%fasl-to-c: expected (fasl-path out-path sym-name is-exe)" (exe? must be a boolean), "cannot open 'in' for reading", "cannot create 'out'". The header declares name[] and name_len.

```scheme
(define (main args) 0)
(dump-fasl "app.fasl")                               ; => #t
(fasl-to-c "app.fasl" "app_fasl.h" "app_fasl" #f)    ; => #t
```

<a id="api-file-remove"></a>
#### `file-remove`

`(file-remove path)`

*since 1.0.0 · PC REPL only*

Delete a host file.

**Returns:** #t when deleted; #f when it does not exist, cannot be deleted or path is not a string. Never an error.

```scheme
(write-file-string "out.tmp" "x")
(file-remove "out.tmp")   ; => #t
(file-remove "out.tmp")   ; => #f
```

<a id="api-file-size"></a>
#### `file-size`

`(file-size path)`

*since 1.0.0 · PC REPL only*

Size of a host file in bytes, or -1.

**Returns:** An integer (bytes); -1 when the file cannot be opened or path is not a string. Never an error.

```scheme
(write-file-string "hello.txt" "hello")
(file-size "hello.txt")     ; => 5
(file-size "missing.txt")   ; => -1
```

<a id="api-system"></a>
#### `system`

`(system command)`

*since 1.0.0 · PC REPL only*

Run a host shell command and wait for it.

**Returns:** The integer C system() returns: the exit code on Windows; on POSIX the wait status (exit code times 256). Error "system: expected command string".

```scheme
(system "gcc --version")
(system "exit 3")   ; => 3
```

<a id="api-write-file-string"></a>
#### `write-file-string`

`(write-file-string path str)`

*since 1.0.0 · PC REPL only*

Create or replace a host file with the bytes of a string.

**Returns:** #t when all bytes were written; #f when the file cannot be created. Error "%write-file-string: expected (filepath string)" when an argument is not a string.

```scheme
(write-file-string "version.txt" "1.0.0\n")   ; => #t
```
